review:
Really solid!

Innovative, interesting, fluid, dynamic co-op design revolving around the 3 tools to repair and apply statuses to enemies/terrain. Your gun is only 1 part of your kit, teamwork is essential for Hard and higher. 
Died on launch due to, mostly it seems, lack of content. While I agree, there should be more than this, what's there is enough to be enjoyably replayable with different kits, guns, builds, all while progressing through the cosmetic/perk trees. Most of the hate is baseless, to be honest. Look for negative reviews over 1 whiny sentence. 
Peer to peer networking, but requires a constant connection to Remedy servers just to launch, which I think is a bad idea when the Solo play is actually kinda solid. Ziplines feel really clunky. It fails half the time I try to ride them. There isn't much RNG to levels, but what's there is good, and more could be disorienting and detracting to the intended pace of the game (don't want to have too much of the game running around looking for the objective when you're clearly intended to stick together under pressure). Gun animations seem to argue too much with other player actions. There's a period in the reload when you've completed the reload (number full) but the animation isn't finished, and it cannot be interrupted. If you want to grab something, throw a grenade, fire, ADS, or repair something, you cannot for some reason. This is minor, and gladly there's no other examples of this kind of anim fighting. 

If I had to reduce it, I'd call it Payday 2 level design (minor RNG, but after a few runs you'll always know what to do) with DRG co-op design, but there's nothing quite like the full buffet of interplaying systems on display. Just make sure to work and stay together! Lone wolves don't get barrier ;3

[h2]Great, real great![/h2]

But I cannot sincerely recommend purchase. The idea is great, the balance is on it's way, thousands of players are already sold on the world, but the crippling dependency on decrepit servers, hallway-like mission design (which completely betrays the nature and selling point of the Oldest House, even worse than how CONTROL failed to fully utilize this aspect outside of literally one event), the 4 months between a major update and a fairly alright gamemode being added, and how few players there are make this game a true struggle to enjoy even for the most optimistic gamer. It literally averages 7 Steam players. That is joke-level bad! That's how much Payday 3 players say they have total! 

It's really such a shame, but in it's current state, this simply is not worth your money, nor do I think it will be for a long time (year [b]at least[/b] given the current rate of development), unless you have a willing friend and the spare cash.
name: FBC: Firebreak

review:
I like the idea of the game, playing with friends is fun (usually) and FBC: Firebreak is able to provide a quick "jump in, play a bit and jump out" while using Control's universe to provide an unique FPS experience, but the game has various problems which sometimes makes playing the game very frustrating.

[i](I originally played the game first time through Game Pass during July 2025 and later in October bought the game on sale. This review takes both states of the game into account).[/i]
Also need to point out, my review comes from the perspective of a Solo player, but I do enjoy the team play too. The game was not designed around solo play and the developers have stated it.

TL;DR: Game has some good bits and if you are a fan of Remedy's Control, you might enjoy the game's setting. Otherwise the game is just not quite there, there's bugs and game gets repetitive after some time. Solo play is not very good, but it's possible. I don't recommend the game at full price and I don't think it's worth 40€.

[h3]Positives:[/h3]
As mentioned above, FBC: Firebreak is very unique where it mechanically relies on status conditions (wet, on fire, frozen, etc...) to bring a very clever way to playing the game and being "wet" is actually a good thing. Enemies (and players) on fire slowly take damage, frozen condition slows them down (and freezes enemies), electricity is actually quite good way to stun enemies (where it doesn't affect the players as much as you think) and few more. Water is treated as the "universal good element" where drinking from fountains/showering in showers heal you and sprinklers and water [Weapons] "soak" the player, giving them resistance to other elements.

The setting of Control's universe adds a bit of that "SCP" spice into the mix, where you aren't dealing with any supernatural forces, but sticky notes that are quite lethal in large amounts, ever spreading goo that blocks everything, sentient skill lifts with extreme cold temperatures and living furnace? (which is not a good thing if it gets out of control). So as a loyal "office" employee of the Bureau, it's your job to scrap in the water cannon, grab a weapon and go deal with the anomalies. Also, the elevator arrives faster if you spam the button, hint hint. Also, you are not going to be using the top of the line or the most traditional weaponry, so get used to it :)

Each player is equipped with a dedicated crisis kit with unique tool and a role in the team, though don't worry if you accidentally stack the same kit as every problem can be dealt by anyone, specific kits just do it a lot faster. The game also features a "special meter", which is your crisis kit's special weapon that can wreck havoc were it in the form of a gnome that creates thunderstorms, teapot that turns your water cannon into a fire cannon or piggy bank that causes vortexes.

One highlight I do have to point is the "resonant perk system" where players are able to select a "3rd tier" of a perk (1st tier provides "weak" version of the perk, "2nd provides strong"), which shares the perk with team-mates as long as they are close-ish to each other, which can be a very handy in coordinated teams (maybe you want to play as a support person and other other players pick lots of perks while you provide few important ones). 

I also like how easily the player is able to restock ammo from the ammo desks.
And while the tasks require to do a mini-game to complete (tap Q or E in certain order shown on the screen), I kinda like it and the environmental hazards can be put out by doing the mini-game (where failing will hurt, but that's why you need to be precise and not spam the keys).

[h3]Neutrals:[/h3]
Game can get repetitive as there aren't that much variety and any variety the game has is very quickly experienced. When playing with other players, there aren't (at the moment) good ways to communicate with the other players as the game lacks a voice chat (pings and quick voice lines can help and when have played with friends, we usually are in a voice call via discord or equivalent services), but having something in the game would be handy. I am not sure about the game progression as most of the perks and equipment

Another aspect that goes into neutral is the "resonant" and "shield system" where closer you are with your team-mates, stronger your shield is, which encourages staying together. Though in some cases I am not sure if this is a good feature as in some cases it can be very dangerous to be together if the enemies manage to surprise the players, or rush with large amounts of enemies... or throw explosives which force players to move, which can lead into tough spots. 

Solo play is... decent. Where playing solo the game feels a bit more responsive, you really miss the team-mates tools to do certain tasks faster. But the solo experience dives down very quickly when the enemies start ramping up and more waves keep appearing while you're trying to do tasks. Hard solo difficulty is manageable, but it really depends what you are supposed to do. If you have to fix things, you are screwed.

[h3]Negatives:[/h3]
Personally, the biggest problem the game has is consistency and many bugs that frustrate. Healing in the game isn't instant and takes a moment before it kicks on, which can be a very serious problem as I have very consistently experienced cases where I'm close to dying and about to heal with a shower or with a water grenade, but I die because the healing didn't being immediately.
Another problem is enemies are very difficult to hit as they tend to flail around a lot and flying enemies are pain to shoot down (even with precision weapons). And also, let's give one of the flying enemies the ability to throw grenades that are hard to notice as the UI element warning about the grenade blends very easily on the screen and deals a lot of damage. Also, those enemies have near perfect aim, where they will (especially in solo) tear your shield and health apart. And on top of that, they stagger you.

Another problem with the game with enemies are... there are so many of them. Every so often you encounter enemy spawns that keep overwhelming the players and they just keep coming and especially on final objective they just keep coming.
And what is even more annoying than millions of enemies appearing to ruin your day? Those enemies breaking the things you are supposed to FIX in order to progress. I have no idea who thought it was wise to let the enemies break the things you are supposed to fix in order to complete the mission!?!  (I had a mission which lasted over an hour because enemies kept breaking the valves I was supposed to fix and even when I ran out of reinforcements, the reinforcement cool-down was so short enough I was able to push through it until I eventually failed because I ran out of reliable healing).

More problems to add to the list are weird menu UI behaviour, some crashes, unable to pick objects if they slightly go inside the world terrain (I have lost so many resources because I couldn't pick them up even though they seemed like I could) and game balance relying too much on "Here's a wave of enemies that feels like 2-3 waves worth of enemies. Have fun"

[hr][/hr]
I really want to enjoy the game and I have enjoyed the game so far, but there are just some days when things don't work or it drives me so mad that I don't want to play the game anymore. It has potential, but execution is not great nor consistent. I hope the developers manage to fix the problems.

For the price, I don't think the game is worth 40€, probably 30€ max after the majority of the problems have been fixed. I'm not sure if I would recommend it on sale either. If you get the game, I highly recommend playing it with friends as solo is not as well balanced. If you can try the game on Game Pass, maybe give it a try... maybe.

review:
[h2]For the price, and what it offers. I don't think its worth it, multiplayer is also pretty dead. 
Most i connect to have an icon showing they're cross-platform and not on steam.[/h2]

I enjoy the setting of the world, the tasks and everything is more interesting than what i've seen in similar games. 
With that said, the game is also VERY confusing if you get into it for the first time. I will admit i was fiddling with settings because i accidentally screwed something up and had to restart the game, and when i did i didn't get the tutorial popping up for me again and couldn't re-play it.
So the tutorial might go through some of the basics, i am aware of this going into the review which is why i focus more on the [i]"logic"[/i] of things in the game. 

[h2]-Fire[/h2]
This is the most baffling thing to me, because the game has a thing where enemies on fire [b]hurt you more[/b] it does damage the enemies but if you have a fire damaging effect you better be killing them quick after you gave them that fire damage or they'll be returning the favour two-fold. Yet, the special attack of the Splash kit is to make the water gun spray fire instead, igniting enemies, friendlies and you alike. And since its your watergun doing it, you can't soak people if you actually set them ablaze, so i just never use that ult. There's also fire damage modifiers for weapons and a fire grenade and just... Why? 
Fire is kind of treated like "Fire, bad. Water, good!" in this game so why the hell do you then give players some fire damage weapons?! Just have them swear off fire entirely, don't touch it, if you see it remove it. Or at the least do something like how Vermintide 2 has the Skaven shoot green warp fire, while the hero Sienna shoots regular fire. So you can tell good fire from bad fire. That way the player can deal a special fire to the enemies [i](Maybe a graphite mixed fire since graphite seems to be the bane of the Hiss' existence?)[/i] that only damage them and not buff them. 

[h2]-Water[/h2]
In this game, water is healing, but for some reason only at certain times. Like in shower stations, from faucets and from a watercooler. But when shot from the Splash kits gun it just soaks you and give you the wet effect. I understand its for balacing reasons, the water gun with its fire rate being able to heal would be quite OP. But its just BS that it does nothing. Like, can't it at least do pitiful low but still some healing? Why is water different from water? 

[h2]-Highlighting items[/h2]
You will have tasks in this game which involve you grabbing or destroying items. These are worthlessly highlighted though, getting only a square marker once you are close to them. 
The maps in this are quite large and you are often assaulted by endless waves of enemies until the task is done. It doesn't give you breathing room. So running around, leaving cover only to aimlessly look for a task among so many other things, is a confusing mess. What they instead should have done is Left 4 Dead's old highlighting system.
Where it gives glowing contrours of the item and you can see it through walls. This means that if you get to a area where you need to grab 10 different things, you can see them and the challenge only becomes getting to them through all the enemies.
Especially things like the corrupted items. 
For context: 
Corrupt items are a game modifier where a item spawn in the area that boosts enemies, debuff you or breaks things  constantly that you'll need to fix. You need to find this item and destroy it for the modifier to disappear.
Now these items vary but the worst one of them is f*cking stapler that zooms around like a rabid mouse.
And these things can only be killed with a special item, a Graphite Grinder, that you also need to run around and look for. And once you have it, its ammo is limited so you can't miss the item too much.
And these corrupted items are NOT HIGHLIGHTED! So someone has to run around and find the graphite grinder and then run around more to find the corrupted item and destroy it. 
While carrying the grinder you can't fire your weapons too, and while the thing does damage enemies keep in mind what i said. Limited ammo.It grinds down the graphite in like 4-5 seconds of uninterupted firing, and you get about 3 graphite blocks. So make it count.

[h2]-Movement and interactions[/h2]
More than once i've had issues in this game related to the movement and interactions of it. The specials of all kits all involve something that the player needs to deploy. But the frankly idiotic thing about this is you need to stand still and let this animation play out of your character dropping the item, which takes like 2-3 seconds.
These items can be the difference between life and death. I don't mind the animation playing out, but if me and the team is running away from a group of enemies, i want to be able to activate the item and keep walking away from them, then i can stop and activate it. I don't want to stop, place the item, activate it and then run. 
If you try to place an item as you are moving, they will play the animation but not place the actual item, but they'll still automatically swap your weapon out for your class tool that's used to activate it. 

I think the game shows potential but it has a lot of things that just makes combat awkward and not fluent, the readability of it is just... Off. 
Its a weird world, that's the intention and i like that. But in return that means that objectives, elements and all that need to be grounded somewhat and not be [i]"Some water heal, some water don't"[/i] and [i]"Fire make enemies stronger, here use thing to set enemies on fire"[/i]
They should also lower the price down to about €20. 
For three classes, nine weapons and about 5-6 missions for €40? Nah man.
And its not fun playing alone so it needs multiplayer to survive. Currently i struggle to connect to a server where it doesn't lose connection or glitch out and connects me to someone's lobby but i can't ready up 
(The button isn't there for me to click)

The game apparently had a rough start and by a look of the numbers, its pretty dead in the water.
I do hope they work on it but the things i feel it needs to improve it are probably harder to implement than just a quick patch. I do hope they do though because at its current clunky state and its price, i don't see those player numbers rising anytime soon.
I got the game as a gift from a friend who wanted to play it. And him and our 3rd friend have pretty much dropped it. Its only me left, and i wasn't even the one who paid for it.

This is how much I love Farming Simulator, but THIS...VERSION...should never have been published:

1) The A.I. if you want to call it that, is atrociously bad. This is simply the DUMBEST version of FS. 

2) The farm is 5ft in front of the harvester, the harvester will BACK UP in a FULL CIRCLE, in the opposite direction, all the way to the edge of the plot, this can take several minutes, eating away your monthly hours.

3) The vehicles SEEK OUT poles, trees, plants, railings, fences, walls, even people walking to break the AI's pathing, and simply stop working.

4) ANYthing can BREAK the AI's pathing, in some cases "nothings" can break the AI's pathing, invisible whatever's that the vehicles literally animate running over.

5) Workers follow the most ridiculous paths to get anything done, making full circles just to continue on the up/down paths, they go OUTSIDE the field of work EVEN though you have “Stay on field” checked, and always end up stuck on something. The simple mission of delivering to the Silo and returning to the spot of deployment is even screwed up. Say you worked one field, and then MANUALLY moved the grain cart tractor combo to another spot near another field (WITH return to Starting location turned OFF) on the OTHER side of the map, and send it on a deliver grain task. After it completes said mission the dang Grain cart combo will go ALL THE WAY BACK, to the original field and THEN say its “TOO FAR AWAY” to complete the task you assigned it. I mean WTH?!?

6) Even “COURSEPLAY” cannot save this smoking trash heap of a game. The Grain cart combo gets STUCK next to the Combine every time. Touching NOTHING, yet in collision mode. Making NO attempts at rolling back to correct the error, just sitting there, 10 minutes one time before I noticed it. So I said, well, the Combine has the “Combine Self-unloading” thanks to Courseplay, So i'll use that...right??? NO! The combine AI will unload the grain into the grain cart, and then BACK INTO said Grain cart, and get STUCK!!! You gotta be “F” kidding me. Triple A companies have become absolute SH*TPILE's and should be bankrupted out of business in favor of the smaller guys/girls, because their products are FAR superior! I'm not supporting ANY other Triple A products until they are PROVEN good and YEARS later have longevity to back up that fact.

review:
So, after having played this game for just about 90 hours, I am finally feeling educated enough to do a review. Personally, I am mostly playing the game for the horses, but I have also tested out a lot of other thing in the game. I have a thing or two to say about this game. 

1. Do not buy it. If you love supporting developers that don't care about anything other than the income, sure - go ahead. But if you actually are looking for a good game? Pick another. I will never recommend Farming Simulator 25 to anyone - not in the state it is. Its whacky, laggy, glitchy - and in its essentials just a reskin from the Farming Simulator 22. 

2. It's just not reaching its potential. Unfortunately, this can happen to games in the lead, especially without competitors - such as Farming Simulator 25, or any other FS game for that matter. They live on hype and loyalty, and they don't really care about improving their game, create longlost features everyone have wanted or fix super-identifiable bugs. They just simply don't care enough about their own game. As long as they earn enough, they're good.

3. If you buy it for the horses...Believe me, you will be greatly disappointed. The horses...Are simply not horses. They are literally just full of nothingness, and bugs. You can't properly care for them or ride them. Horses suddenly just vanishes. At this point they are unplayable without mods. And having mods to be able to just be able to play with horses is both hilarious and humiliating. And if you are like me, you might look at all the details and effort put into the horses. Well, all I can promise you is get ready for horrible and unrealistic animations. I promise you, you will be taken out of the immersion immediatly. 

4. If you buy it for animals. Just expect them to be boring as hell, living like soul-less machines just... being there. No thought have been put into them, they are just another step in the production chain. Although, yes, Farming Simulator 25 (and prior games) is more about the farming, they have in fact added both animals and forestry - and it is the latter they have put the juice into. The amount of no effort put into the animals is not exactly shocking, the developers are known to be lazy. Like why on earth do you add baby animals to each animal type except horses?!? Laziness or just out of your scope? If the latter, you best turn around and implement your animals promptly. And why, why is there no genders on the animals? Like, you could put in a snippet of code and the game would just feel a tad more on earth - but no no, it is not important enough.

I could write more, but as I am mostly into the animals aspect, I'm going to stop here. Just TLDR: I regret supporting these developers. Their game is literally just a overpriced piece of garbage. Thank you for reading my review and rant from a horse gamer and animal enthusiast.

review:
IT'S ALWAYS THE SAME... Hear me out.

I mean, yeah, it is a farming simulator as we know it. However, I don't really see much difference between fs25 and fs22. Two main differencies are ground deformation (we will get to that shortly) and improved graphics.

-- Famous breathtaking ground deformation --
So, the long loooong waited feature that should've been in farming simulator like many yeras ago... Spintires did it perfectly in 2014, why couldn't the Giants even in 2025? It is a farming simulator or atleast it's supposed to be. This game is so arcade-ish that calling it a "simulator" is like spiting in a face of other great simulators out there. I mean, if it is called a simulator, why we cannot interract with stuff, like we could pull the levers in tractors or push the buttons in vehicles.. that's what is missing from this game (I aint calling it a simulator no more). "Ground deformation" is what Giants are calling it. I only see a slight bend of a flat surface and that's what you call a ground deformation?! This is not what players expect in 2025!

-- Ultra hyper photo realistic improved graphics --
NO! Adding cloud shadows with fog that'll eat up 15% of your CPU power is not what an enhanced graphics are supposed to be. Fix your g☺dd♥mn physics and gameplay first, then work on graphics. I mean, yeah.. the graphics are SOMEWHAT better compared to fs22. But sweet god in heavens. The physics are still awful. The've been awful in fs22, 19, 17, 15 and I could go on and on.

-- Awful physics --
Now let's talk about the physics mentioned above. Why do I think they are awful? Vehicles have little to no kinetic energy. Every vehicle feel so cumbersome. They've had theese weird physics in.. every.. other.. farming.. "simulator"... Another thing, stacking many bales on one another sometimes makes them behave strangely. They tend to start wiggle and then blast in every direction (rip 30+ mins of manual bale stacking). This bug (or maybe a feature) was also present in every other fs.

-- Great vehicle "damage" (proposed in fs19 and still awful today) --
You slam into a tree at 90 km/h, suddenly you stand still and there is no damage to the vehicle you're driving or to a tree. Try that in real life if you get the same results. ;)
They've seriously just put a blue marker and expect us to believe that it is a vehicle damage marker. LOL, no! It is supposed to be called a vehicle maintanance marker, not damage. There is no such thing as damage in this game.

-- Very realistic character controls --
They somehow screwed up even a feature that was working just fine in fs22. WOW! I understand that they were trying to "improve" jumping and moving physics. However, they've made a step back with this one. The character controls now feel more like controlling a sluggish man with crippled legs. And jumping? Oh my god in heavens... Don't even try to! If you sprint and jump, you'll lose like 70% of kinetic energy mid-air. They've also added a cooldown for jumping. WHY?!?! LIKE WHYYYY? It's sooo annoying. Character controls were just far better in previous games.

-- Unbelievably exciting gameplay --
Don't take me wrong. I seriously enjoyed playing fs17, 19 and 22 (I have like 250+ hours on each one). Don't tell me that this game is not for me. Why it is so that the best means of money making are also the most boring ones? Smallest tools possible and hours of driving on the same field. Nope, not doing that for a 100th time.

-- Amazing new features --
Doing rice is boring af. So is doing the spinach, peas and all new crops and even not talking about the fact that almost all new vehicles are an end-game stuff. And oh, I almost forgot. New animals, you say? Buffalos? Really? An endgame stuff.. again.

-- Conclusion --
Giants had such a great opportunity to bring us something new and unique. And they've bring us only slightly better graphics and slight bending of plain surface which they called a ground deformation. In my eyes, farming simulator had become an economic-grinding simulator. Like it is not about farming anymore. It is about just grinding for money. Every farming game from Giants feels the same for last 6 years. I don't want it like this anymore. I'm tired of this.

review:
It’s 2025 and FS25 still runs on a very old engine.
That’s honestly the biggest problem.

The game has potential, but the graphics feel stuck somewhere between FS15 and FS17. Almost nothing in the world reacts to light properly, the trees don’t move, the foliage is dead, and the whole map feels static and flat. It’s not “stylized,” it’s just outdated.

The worst part?
Most of the Steam screenshots look way better than the actual game. They’re heavily edited, downsampled, captured in a debug mode or simply not representative of normal gameplay. Once you play it yourself, everything looks overexposed, washed out, and with zero atmosphere.

Even with ReShade you can’t fix the core issues, because the engine doesn’t support any modern features. No raytracing, no GI, no proper sky lighting, no volumetric shadows, nothing. Other simulators moved forward (UE4, UE5, HDRP, etc.), but FS25 still uses DX11 and old screen-space tricks that break with FOV or camera movement.

The trees are a perfect example:
No proper animation, no believable lighting, no depth, no softness, no scattering. They look almost the same as in FS15. And when the environment looks dead, the whole game feels dead.

FS25 plays fine, but visually it’s extremely outdated.
If you expect modern graphics in 2025, you will be disappointed.

Don't forget the wood, it's unplayable.

review:
Played FS22 since it came out & I waited quite some time before picking this one up since I had other games to play. I'm a bit disappointed though.

Issues:
- Game tends to soft crash during saves fairly regularly. I have verified that I have no mod conflicts per my game logs, but there are a fair amount of seemingly outdated mods since textures or paint jobs aren't loading once the equipment is purchased.
- It's already been a week since the last update & I've only seen one 3rd party mod updated, it seems like the mod authors aren't active.
- I found a mod by Giants that has caused my game to crash multiple times, each time I had purchased a MF large tractor. Which is dumb since the Dev added it to the library as free content. It shouldn't break the game.
- Mods seem to not load into existing saves. So in my experience, I had to wipe my save & start over to see the new mods loaded in.
- There was an issue that I had regarding the Shader compiling. Somehow the "shader_<insert random characters here>" file got corrupted after the first few launches of the game after it had soft crashed multiple times in a row. For example, if I remember correctly, the game crashed 5 times in 30min of attempting to play, but it would crash during the load screen. Deleting this shader file & wiping all save games from the C:\Users\<username>\Documents\My Games\FarmingSimulator2025 did resolve that particular issue, but that's ridiculous that I had to even go that far to resolve a game loading issue after verifying game files didn't work.
- There's literally a 3rd party mod in the mod library that supposedly attempts to resolve the game save crashing by making autosave more frequent. However, in my experience, it doesn't work.

Biggest takeaway:
- I really like FS22 & was hoping that FS25 would be a bit more polished. However, I see that, even though I waited just over a year to buy this game, it still isn't in a solid spot based on my experience & frustrations in troubleshooting. At this time, I would NOT recommend spending money on this game. If Giants fixes this game save crashing issue, like a responsible & in-tune developer would, then I'd be willing to change my mind & edit my review to reflect this change.

review:
Overall, this game delivers on its promises: you can farm and drive licensed tractors. So far, so good.

But oh boy, the rest of it is just a disgrace of low-effort incompetence and neglect you’d expect in a license-filled slop game. This wouldn’t be so bad if this weren’t the fourth—or maybe third—installment in this series.

The menus are a hacky compromise to avoid making their own PC/console UI, meaning that on PC, navigating them—for example, looking at mods—is a pain-inducing experience. The constant reminder of what each button does is also heavily oriented toward consoles. In-game, this continues, but I give it a pass since there’s a lot of stuff to control.

In-game, the next big thing you will encounter is performance. It’s called “(20)25” but has so little modern optimization, and it runs only on one core. So even if you have a monster, beefy machine to run this, you will have bad performance, lags, and spikes. It’s horrendous how badly this thing runs on modern hardware.

The overall gameplay is also plagued with console controls. The map is a mystery that I think is basically not properly finished, and controlling AI workers is a pain. But as far as I’ve read, they are already far better than in previous installments.

The driving physics are passable but sometimes feel really shit due to performance hitches, and they often do not behave either like a simulator or a casual driving experience. Wheels won’t return to neutral positions, for example—but sometimes they do. Oversteering with keyboard and mouse is a constant struggle.

Multiplayer works, but also rather badly—and even consumer-hostile. If you want to host your own private dedicated server, you need to buy an additional license, as the game prevents you from running the game twice or downloading the server separately like 99% of other games allow. This is the biggest and unforgivable flaw. This is something I have not encountered yet in any game I’ve played and hosted myself! Oh, and of course there is no Linux server either; it all must be run under Windows, which eats performance. Really shitty product.

One thing that really stands out, however, is the enormous amount of mods this game has and is able to run. We did a test run with over 2,500 mods for additional vehicles and stuff, and it ran no worse than with 450 mods—or none. This is really cool!

All in all, the overall pain we had before even starting to play, and the constant reminders and bad experiences while playing, clearly make me not recommend this “product.”

TL;DR: Ein Spiel gemacht von BAUERN für BAUERN.

review:
Edit: Im glad we have exhausted the content that it had before they added tons more bugs to the game.
Also im not convinced about the direction the development took.
Coop would need far more features to be worthwhile and the base gameplay needed a ton more mechanics, better AI, more options like having two restaurants and so on.
Instead they add stuff like a bad PvP mode.
But bugs are left unfixed.
It still doesnt matter how the food looks, often not even if its hot served or from a day before.
I can still prepare 20 dishes, store them in a fridge and then microwave the entire day to still get max ratings.
The ultimate skill in this game is to manage 10 microwaves.
Theres still a ton of metrics missing, like visual appeal, dish quality and the AI wont have any interaction with your restaurant besides sitting down and eating.
They arent acting realistic in any way, like looking at stuff, making a selection or speaking with each other.

They need to refocus their development very fast.
But i see that 2025 will already have them finish 1.0 and i assume thats because they want to wrap it up and call it a day.
MORE dishes or restaurants wont make this more fun.
It needs more mechanics that make it more complex and deeper in terms of management and customer variance.
What about Service Quality as a factor thats totally missing?

Add more proper mechanics, not just noise.


---------------------------------

Its a really fun game, if they fix some quirks, bugs and design issues it can become stellar.
Add more recipes and options to create food or manage your guests and its possibly the best food simulator out there, especially due to coop.

Bugs is a bit vague so i describe what type of bugs appeared to me:
- I sliced potatoes to "sliced potatoes", basically wedges. Wanted to create Pomme De Frittes. I placed the wedged into the fryer, but nothing would happen, the wedges wouldnt cook/fry/heat up.
I realized i needed to slice the wedges again, picked them out and sliced them, placed them back into the fryer. The fryer now constantly lists that it has 4 sliced potatoes inside, which ofcourse it doesnt.
This stays for the rest of the game.
Its these types of bugs. Clipping things, physic based bugs, stuff that doesnt get removed or stucks in the air.

Problem 1: The game should allow me to place wedges into the fryer and they should heat up.
In general the game doesnt give you a lot of leeway and freedom to create food or "interpret" recipes. Maybe i wanted to fry wedges instead of Pommes and maybe the guests would love that far more.
Which leads to Problem 2.

Problem 2: The guests are one dimensional. 
They can only come in (and you can only open your shop/restaurant once you have cooked something) once you selected a recipe and serve it.
And they come with one of the offered dishes in mind.
That makes sense, since you do the same in a restaurant in real life.
But that also means i can only offer the food, the game allows me to offer.
So i have potatoes and i have chicken and i have pepper bells. But i can only create chicken with fries and (unsliced) peppers.
I cant, for example, make it Chicken Stripes with Wedges and Sliced Pepper with Sour Cream.
I cant serve the Chicken Filet with Salted Cooked Potatoes instead of fries.
I cant combine ingredients with each other to create a result and the people entering my restaurant wont react to what they get.
Even when we messed up recipes by missing an ingredient etc, they were super happy with it.
I think i never had a situation in my first 2 hours, where a customer went out unhappy with what he or she got, even if burnt stuff or cold fries from the day before.

In a great game, if i could wish for something to drastically improve, i could customize the recipes or outright combine ingredients to create my own.
More like Pizza Connection but without being limited to Pizza.
Let me cook potatoes, grill a steak, a tomato and a pepper, place the stuff on a dish with a bit of ketchup and serve it and then have customers come in, each with their individual taste and preferences randomly applied, eat it and rate it or even leave the restaurant again when they see it wont meet their taste (vegetarians etc? to give an example).

More like a mix between the food creation system of Pizza Connection and the customer mechanic from Rollercoaster Tycoon.
Create something, present it with a certain style and then clash that creation with your customers expectations.
 
Problem 3:
You can cheese the game.
Due to the bugs you can break the game too.
For example, if you go outside and stand in the path of an NPC he will stop and the game code will search for a new path.
Doing that you can lead NPCs into your restaurant.
I just stood outside and blocked them infront of our door to lead them in.



In general the game lacks choice and options combined with some depth in areas that are important to be deeper.
I think customers in a game about serving dishes to people are an integral part i expect to be as deep and complex as they can.
They need to have "opinions" about your restaurant, its outside style, its inside style, the food or the prices (ah yes, you cant adjust prices at all), the taste, the service and even the menu (only mains, sidedishes?, deserts? Drinks?).

But they really dont.

Same goes for the cooking. Its flat. You have predefined recipes and thats it.
You cant even.....empty a cooking pot.
I poured too much water into it when creating soup and i was screwed. Cant pour out water to fix my fault. 
Cant even scrap it entirely (empty the entire pot).
Same goes for heat.
You cant tell whether food is hot or not.
I had a soup pot and wanted to keep it warm/reheat by putting it on the stove.
But when serving it the game told me it was only 53% hot enough, reducing the rating.
But i couldnt tell how hot the stuff was before serving it to people.
Also cant take it out again to reheat it more.

Heat is also basically the only dimension food has.
Theres no skill or other influences to my dishes.
I cant experiment with spices (chili on my chicken? No? Why not?), i cant become better at slicing stuff or preparing meat etc.
It all just comes down to timing in the heating process.
Your only dimension of how good your food will be, depends on how well cooked the ingredients are and how fast you serve it (as it cools down).




If they fix these things and expand the game there, its incredible.

As of now, i recommend it becuase its low priced, has coop, is fun (still) and offers some content.
But due to the above issues theres lacking replayability, lacking options, lacking depth and thus lacking experimentation.

I really hope the devs keep going, as the basis it has is great and has potential.

review:
This game is a buggy mess. When collision issues aren't causing you to waste water and soup, you'll see customers completely ignoring table collision to walk through them. Plates sometimes disappear completely when picking them up or putting them down. 

If you bought individual plates and wash them, they won't be placed into the clean dish bin, and you have to grab them from the sink while you're still "washing" it to remove it, else it will go back into the dirty plate bin and become dirty again. Sometimes you can't put individual plates back in the plate shelf, other times you can.

Plates also somehow end up in the clean plate bin while they're still dirty... *after* you just washed it. This causes you to prioritize the "dirty" plate from the clean bin and repeatedly wash it in an infinite loop. The only way to fix it is by putting the "dirty" plate back into the plate shelf. 

These are just a few of the bugs I've experienced while playing the game with my girlfriend. Beyond that, the lackluster English makes it difficult to take the game seriously at times.

When it comes to simulator games, my expectations are typically very low because of the experiences I've had with them in the past. Games like this one only lower that bar further and make it difficult for me to go in with an open mind.

Do yourself a favor and look for something else. The core game here is fine, but the bugs make it a miserable experience that I can't, in good conscience, recommend to anyone.

review:
PERSONAL FEELINGS:
I played the first Killing Floor game as a kid, and it really scared me. The monsters' appearances, sounds, and atmosphere were perfect for the time period. The second game was a bit more modern, but still felt like a sequel to Killing Floor. This third game, however, was a mix of Doom + Gears of War + Dead Space. I played it like the Killing Floor skin mod had been added to another game.

OVERALL REVIEW:
In previous games, you felt confident as your character progressed, but in this game, the weapon impact and body damage are very weak, and instead of providing a challenging gameplay experience, it becomes tedious. The dash system doesn't work to prevent damage because you're definitely taking damage. The gun's appearance is definitely sloppy and space-themed. The inability to pick up limited syringes and ammo boxes is a complete disappointment. The game tried to combine the survival mechanics of Resident Evil with the mind-numbing, just-shoot-and-hunt-the-monsters mechanics of Doom, but it's completely incompatible. If you run out of syringes, you have no alternative, and likewise, if you run out of money, you have no alternative to pick up ammo. (The AMMO BAG is useful for multiplayer.)

CREATURE REVIEW
Siren, Fleshpound, Husk, and Screamer are well-designed, but Clot and Crawler are smooth, air-filled jelly, like Demi Eligos's cutest creatures from Evil Dead the Game. Furthermore, even if Screamer and Fleshpound lose their slow, intimidating gait and don't take damage, they still chase you furiously, and your damage-dealing time is very limited. Husk has received a major mobility boost. Also, why does Bloat run, and his acid-spraying behavior is hilarious. Executions feel like stabbing through the air, not like hitting something solid, so they're unsatisfying. MOST IMPORTANTLY, WHY ARE THERE NO STALKERS IN THIS GAME?

FINAL WORDS:
The game throws random creatures at you, and you try to kill them with useless dashes and damaging weapons like bead guns.

I'm going to play this game because I love the genre and because it has a system for XP, character, skill, and weapon upgrades. If it weren't for these, I'd refund the game.

I hope the old developer returns and the next game is a KILLING FLOOR (2009) REMASTERED OR REMAKE (THE GAME KF FANS ACTUALLY WANT)

55/100

review:
If you want the tldr of what I think about the game, it is barely a 4/10, just narrowly escaping a 3/10 rating. It is slightly worse than kf1 and noticeably worse than kf2. Do not buy this game.

Okay now for the long answer: The best thing about this game is the moment-to-moment gameplay. It is better than either of the two previous Killing Floor games. That is literally the only thing I can definitively say is better about this game. Everything else about it is either not improved or somehow worse than before.

Killing floor throughout its lifetime has always suffered the curse of having good gameplay with nothing else to tag alongside that gameplay. It's why despite me being a big fan of both the 1st and 2nd game, I can really only rate them a 5 and 6 out of ten, respectively. They have good gameplay, but nothing else, and without any replay value, its gameplay becomes a harder selling point, especially when as you play those games more you become more in tune with all of their flaws and annoying quirks.

Kf3 decides that in order to tackle that replayability issue, that it should have a crafting system for weapon altering mods, that also have RNG based bonuses, that requires you to upgrade to the max with resources that you must ALSO grind for in game in order to access said bonuses. Oh, and you cannot exchange your more common resources for the rarer ones, so have fun grinding your ass off for gray matter and ESPECIALLY biosteel. Seriously, Deep Rock Galactic already has a resource exchange system, and Darktide used to be infamous for having some of the worst RNG grinds/crafting systems ever seen in a video game, so the fact that the devs decided to go this route while also half-assing it is baffling. The only good thing I can say about this crafting system is that recycling mods gives you back most of the resources you spent to craft it, but this wouldn't even be an issue at all if you could just... exchange your more common resources for the rarer ones.

Oh, speaking of grind, have fun playing normal and hard for the first 25 levels of each and every one of your perks, cause you do not have the damage or tankiness required to deal with Hell-on-Earth enemies before that point. And the leveling system takes nearly twice as long as kf2's, Hooray! Honestly I'd rather deal with kf1's leveling system, because at least there leveling up gave you a substantial boost in your abilities, can't say the same here. You not only have to grind for levels to get skills, you have to grind for skillpoints to then upgrade those skills to make them more potent, AS IF WE NEEDED ANY MORE FUCKING GRINDING IN THIS GAME. Oh, and the cherry on top is that you aren't allowed to swap skills between waves whatsoever, something that Kf2 and even kf1 allowed you to do. This is literally a downgrade in every single way.

And even though the gameplay may be fun, most of the weapons sure as hell aren't. The feedback for most of them are terrible, and on Hell-on-Earth, you only get a few options to use: The Vulcan, G33 with enfeeble grenades, the Striek with quad barrel and enfeeble slugs, or the scar. And you must always have your upgrades geared towards damage, bonuses included, because the more damage you deal, the faster you kill, which means the less time something has to attack you. And because bonuses are entirely RNG based, that means you could potentially grind for a ton of resources to get parts with specific bonuses, AND THEN JUST NOT GET THEM ANYWAY.

And don't even get me started on the performance issues. Yep, it's built on Unreal 5, and you know what that means: Lots of lag, Lots of PC resource hogging, and crashes. Lots and lots of crashes. I would have more to say about what is wrong with the game, but to be honest with you, the game crashes so much for me that I cannot point out other issues about the game outside of the immediately obvious ones. Mind you, my PC can run Helldivers 2 buttery smooth, 90+ FPS, and that game is INFAMOUS for having godawful performance. Something about Unreal engine 5 just makes games using it perform terribly, and the bad performance alone is why I wouldn't recommend this game.

This game had every opportunity to succeed, and Tripwire fumbled the bag so badly that I honestly do not see any future for this game, and I'm scratching my head over the people who claim otherwise. "Just wait like a year or two bro, it'll be better then!" Have you guys seen the player counts? They are fucking abysmal. As of right now, this game has around 300 concurrent players and a peak of a little over 600. It is BARELY beating out Kf1 right now, a game made almost 14 years ago. So yeah, do not buy this game, and do not listen to anyone who says otherwise, they are either currently high on copium or lying to you.

I was really looking forward to Killing Floor 3, but honestly… this has been one of the most disappointing launches in recent memory (beside PAYDAY3).

The gunplay and atmosphere should be amazing, the core DNA of the franchise is still here, but none of that matters when the game runs like this. Even on a high-end rig, the performance is a disaster. Constant stuttering, random frame drops, and inexplicable input lag plague every match. I’ve tried every combination of graphics settings, driver updates, and even fresh installs, nothing makes it consistently smooth.

Worse yet, the optimization feels completely unfinished. CPU usage is erratic, VRAM spikes for no reason. Some maps even tank the framerate to the low 40s despite “optimized” presets.

It’s frustrating because beneath all the technical mess, there’s a genuinely good game trying to break through. But right now, it’s buried under poor optimization and half-baked polish.

Tripwire needs to take this seriously and push out performance patches fast. Until then, I can’t recommend Killing Floor 3 on PC. Wait for major updates, or for the inevitable “Enhanced Edition” down the road.

review:
Never bought and refunded a game so fast. My reasoning is solely from the fact that the visuals and audio feedback in this game is a MASSIVE downgrade from KF2. Anyone that thinks otherwise has to be lying. And yes, this whole review is JUST about that, not even including the gameplay issues that other reviews mention. I wanted to give this game a chance despite the reviews.

When I'm playing a horde shooter, I'd expect the gameplay to actually pack a punch and feel visceral. KF2 nailed that with the animations, gore, sound design, etc. Same can be said about games like L4D2. When you shoot and slice through gore in those games, it has excellent feedback and makes the repetitive nature of killing the same enemies over and over more fun. The zed animations in 2 were all mocapped by an actor, and you can see the fluidity of the movements in game. KF3? All the animations look stiff as a board. None of the zed animations look like they were mocapped. Just look at ANY zed running animation from KF2 and compare it to the zeds in 3. It is a night and day comparison. Also, most of the guns feel like plastic toys. 

So why does this matter of all things? Cause you'd think that the third installment of a series would be an improvement over the last in some way. I would've been able to let everything else about the game slide if they at least kept the FEEL of the game quality similar / better, but it's just too jarring and distracting to keep me engaged.

So unless they manage to do a massive overhaul of the animation system or something, I can't justify buying this game in its current state. It's honestly kinda sad that fans have waited so long for this only for the game to be released like it is. "But KF2 had a terrible launch too!" Why are we justifying KF3's shortcomings just cause the previous title did the same? Don't we want a finished final product on release? The problem is that this game didn't release as an early access title.

review:
Don't even kid yourself with this game, even after this 'big' update that's come out recently, this game is a spit in the face of anybody who had any attachment to the series and an insult to newcomers.

The cosmetics have both been made worse and uglier - the hi-tech theme was poorly received in KF2, so obviously we'll theme the third game entirely around it! Rather than letting the player to mix and match their cosmetics (or expanding on it) we just got a body slot and a head slot, cosmetics are exclusively tied to the new passes (no special themed rewards from weeklys, vosh crates or random drops) but, that doesn't even matter much when each character is just not that interesting, not real amusing lines, flat personalities that were clearly written with the perk tied character design in mind and a VA change for Foster, which makes me think Scully will have the same. We didn't even get the brit vets of the voicing from the previous games making a return.

But hey, this is all cosmetic, maybe the gameplay saves it? Of course not. If you enjoyed Berserker, you'll be happy to know that it feels worse than it did in the first game, with enemies having their attacks coming out before their animations would suggest (gorefasts being the most frustrating), parrying just feels incredibly awkward and there's only 2 dedicated melee weapons (3 counting the kunai) 1 being a katana and the second being 2 katanas - complete joke. 

This is a good segway though, because why would you use melee on the class that appears to be melee oriented when you can just spec into bleed damage and have some of the highest, no effort global damage boost around! Class identity? What's that? let's just make it so all classes can use everything and have practically 0 reason to ever specialise, it's not like the perks were made for that reason, they were just a vague suggestion clearly. All of the skills feel next to useless minus the few meta ones - why add more if they're all garbage? 3 trees and yet most of them are not even worth looking at.

Core gameplay changes were done, such as removing the weight and thus the inventory system entirely, which helped balancing out the powerful weapons and gave you a reason to think about what you took (on top of choosing things that your perk actually benefited from - but whatever...) wave lengths are gone, now it's always 6 wave, no 4/7/10 anymore - Endless? Objective?(not that I cared for it, but usually sequels should probably have more in it) all MIA. Healing? limited to a certain usage based on skills however this means that battles of attrition will always end in failure since you're limited on how much damage you can take, this also means healing others is exclusively medic weapons now for darts, I don't get this change - why attempt to fix what wasn't broken?

Weapons feel weak and without any real buffs coming from the perks, they stay weak, maybe to push you in the direction of grinding mats for the purpose of applying and upgrading attachments on them to slightly buff their damage numbers and their cost to buy from the trader - I'm not really opposed to this idea, but I dislike how weak everything feels except for a handful of them *cough* vulcan *cough* Either damage tuning needs to be made, or enemy HP needs to be slashed across the board, way too much of the game is spent just backpedalling away from everything - which feels weird, since holding a lane or being Han Solo popping heads in the previous games were great, but feels far less of an option in this one.

Graphically, colours are all washed out, nothing really pops and things can blend together, I don't mind the visual changes on the zeds, but I hate how grey everything appears, it's completely lifeless.

Map design is probably the only thing I don't hate, the maps all feel nice and somebody even remade them in KF2 which lets you enjoy them without the drag of having to play them in their original state.

I should also note that I had 0 ability to finish a multiplayer match because community servers are gone and so are dedicated servers, because we still live in 2007 apparently and I kept disconnecting before any match could even finish. So all my playtime was done solo, which led me thinking that maybe weapons feel so horrible because zed hp isn't scaled, but even then, that means they still feel like shit with multiple players. Community stuff in general is completely absent, I don't think we'll see community skins make a return - mutators are out and goodbye to custom maps I guess. Will they return? who knows and who cares, something tells me this game won't have anybody developing for it anyway.

While there's certainly more to expand on, I'm trying to keep my complaining brief - but last thing I need to touch on is the bosses. They're boring and they have 0 personality. No voice lines, they're just ugly abominations, which is like - yea, fine. But it's just an odd departure from the rest, they're also subject to the same tanky nonsense as the rest of the cast, so it's spent just backpedalling and slowly plinking away their health and hoping they don't smack you around because you have limit healing charges! and to make it even better, you're slow as molasses to incentivise using the dodge, which feels like a move backwards faster button and is just annoying to have to constantly press. The only real time you need to dodge is to avoid the Fleshpounds and their tracking slam attacks and Gorefast stabs, because even if you sidestep before they even start it, they always seem to connect, but whatever - skill issue.

So... yeah. Wait on it for a couple years and come back to an amazing game? Fat chance, I'd wager now this game will be completely abandoned within a year once the team gets axed for it's poor sales. It flopped on launch and I don't see any breath being breathed into it anytime soon and HEY - if only there was community content to keep things alive and fresh. I wonder if that's ever been done before?

Edit: Oh look I forgot to mention, just like the team forgot to push out - that Halloween passed and no themed event in sight, maybe that's another thing we can say got lost in translation.

review:
Dear Tripwire Team,

I’m writing because I’ve been a Killing Floor fan for years — from the mod days through KF2 — and because I genuinely care about this series. My brother and I have over 100 hours each in KF3 and countless more in KF2. We wanted to love this game. But right now, KF3 doesn’t feel like Killing Floor anymore.

1. You Took Away the Heart of the Game
Where is Kevin Clamely? Where’s the weird, dark humor and atmosphere that gave the series personality? KF3 feels sterile — the identity has been stripped out.

The biggest problem: the game revolves entirely around getting a Vulkan. Every perk, every build, every decision feels secondary to that one goal. It’s terrible design. The individuality of perks — the soul of the series — is gone. Ironically, there are essentially no perks in the game; it’s just whichever perk has the better stats on the Vulkan.

Each perk has no clearly defined role anymore, partly because of the weapon-focus meta. There need to be clear trash killers and large zed killers. Right now, each perk has enough hybrid skills that let them do both too well, making perk choice meaningless. For example, there’s no need for a Combat Medic because the buffs they provide aren’t strong enough to justify their presence — they don’t kill anything better than any other perk. And since everyone can use a Medic Pistol with purple darts, the Medic heals no better than anyone else either.

A simple fix: boost perk-specific weapon bonuses to make staying within your perk’s arsenal worth it again. Each perk should feel like an expert with their weapons — just like in KF1 and KF2, where you reloaded faster and did more damage with your perk guns. That gave perks identity and mastery. Right now, it’s often better for a Sharpshooter to use an explosive shotgun or the Vulkan than to use their own arsenals. Bass ackwards.

And please, bring back perk passives. Those small, intrinsic upgrades tied your identity to your class and gave each one a rhythm of growth. Losing them makes leveling feel hollow. The current passives are not acknowledgeable.

2. Encumbrance and Strategic Choice Are Gone
One of the most elegant systems in KF2 was encumbrance. It created genuine strategy and mid-match decision-making — choosing between a powerful but heavy weapon or a flexible loadout with utility.

That ebb and flow between waves — picking mid-tier weapons between levels 2–4, deciding whether to switch loadouts before a boss — mattered. It gave every game personality.

Now, encumbrance is gone, and so are those choices. Every match just becomes a race to the Vulkan, and once you get it, your decisions are over. That’s not progression — it’s monotony.

3. Gameplay Bugs and RNG Madness
We got the Queen Crawler five games in a row.
At a 33% chance per boss, that’s a 1 in 40,000 event. Probably a bug, but it killed morale. My brother and I even made a bet: if it happened again, we’d uninstall. You can guess what spawned next.

And where is Suicidal difficulty? “Hard” is too easy, “Hell on Earth” is a wall. Suicidal was that perfect middle ground — the natural home for players who’d mastered the basics but didn’t want every match to be a punishment.

4. Balance and Combat Feel
Combat feels wrong across the board:

Scrakes are pure bullet sponges now, even with top-end weapons like the Vulkan. The classic KF dynamic — explosives for Fleshpounds, bullets for Scrakes — is gone. It used to reward tactical coordination.

Sharpshooter is borderline useless. Zeds bob and weave too much to land headshots consistently, especially when you’re overwhelmed. Even if you do, the Sharpshooter’s weapons hit like peashooters compared to other perks’ explosive or area-damage options. They should be the fastest at killing large zeds with precision — that’s their purpose — but right now, they get outpaced by nearly everyone. The Engineer’s Ifrit can kill a Fleshpound in three bolts, and the Firebug’s Vulkan can burn one down in two full charges.

Perk roles don’t matter. Every perk can do everything decently well. The lack of specialization makes team composition meaningless.

Why make Scrakes weak to cut damage, then cover them in Zedtech armor that resists cut damage? It’s confusing and counterintuitive.

KF used to reward coordinated play — now it rewards whichever perk can abuse the current meta weapon.

Suggestion: Bring back static perk-specific stats like in KF1 and KF2. Tie reload, damage, and weapon handling bonuses to perk weapons only. That would naturally restore balance and bring back the satisfaction of mastering your role.

And while we’re here — take sidearms away or rework them. The extra slot feels clunky and pointless. Just have two weapon slots and buff pistols to make them viable secondaries instead of filler. Right now, having two primaries bound to one slot just adds frustration.

5. Technical and Interface Frustrations
KF3 runs poorly on every system I’ve tried. It’s visually fine, but the optimization is abysmal for what’s on screen.

And the menus and interface make the experience worse:

The crafting material pool doesn’t appear on the crafting page. You have to back out through several menus just to check your totals.

The weapon part crafting system feels awful. Please make it so we can choose the tier 3 ability instead of grinding endlessly for perfect rolls. The parts make a huge difference in weapon power, and the current system feels more punishing than rewarding.

Sentry activation is inconsistent — sometimes a tap of “E,” sometimes a hold.

The operational budget isn’t visible outside of a match. If I want to test upgrades, I literally have to open a live game or do math by hand. Just add a loadout sandbox in the menu for preplanning.

Add a “Teleport to Chopper” button in the menus. It’s a small quality-of-life thing, but running back to the chopper every single time is tedious.

KF2’s menus were clunky but functional. KF3’s feel like work.

6. Character Writing and Tone
The voicelines are rough. KF2 had charm — personality mixed with grim humor. KF3’s dialogue sounds tone-deaf, especially the Engineer, who lectures about “improving zeds” as scientific projects in a post-apocalyptic world. It breaks immersion completely — why would the protagonists be suggesting improvements to the monsters they’re fighting to survive against?

7. The Grind and Progression
Something changed under the hood, because the XP grind has slowed dramatically.
At launch, I leveled Assault and Engineer to 30 in about 15–20 hours each. Now, after 50 hours of Firebug, I’m still not 30. It feels like progress got throttled silently, and it kills long-term motivation.

The game shouldn’t be about the grind to level 30 — the game should start once you reach it. The fun begins when perks are fully unlocked and team synergy shines. Please make XP gain faster so players can get to the real experience sooner.

8. The One Thing You Got Right
KF3 finally lets me queue privately with my friends. That’s a huge improvement over KF2, where randoms could join mid-match — even on the last wave — beg for dosh, and ruin the boss prep because nobody could armor up or reload properly.

You also stopped low-level players from dropping into high-wave lobbies, which used to break pacing and team balance. Credit where it’s due — this feature is one of the best quality-of-life changes in the entire franchise.

9. Final Thoughts
All of this comes from a place of love and deep familiarity with Killing Floor.
KF1 and KF2 still pull thousands of players daily because they feel cohesive — perks have personality, teamwork matters, and the experience flows.

KF3 stripped that away and replaced it with an unfocused weapon-upgrade grind that undermines the very things that made Killing Floor special.

Please, give perks their meaning back. Restore encumbrance and strategic choice. Fix the boss RNG, rebalance the combat roles, and optimize the engine.

The series deserves better than this.

review:
Tras completar el pase de batalla que el juego contiene, y con 60 horas de juego, reflejaré mi valoración.

- Si el usuario no dispone un ordenador muy moderno, el tiempo promedio para entrar al juego es de 5-10 minutos para cargar todos los recursos del mismo, en caso contrario inicia rápidamente.

- Prácticamente es un juego como si se encontrase en fase beta (o gamma si existiera) pues tiene innumerables bugs que afectan al gameplay. De entre los errores del amplio abanico que he tenido el placer de encontrar, destacan los siguientes: expulsión de la partida por conexión con el servidor o por el anti cheat, el mapa se vuelve oscuro o no deja de temblar, el boss final de la partida no spawnea, no spawnear con el arma inicial en el multijugador, colisiones imperfectas al compartir dinero con otros jugadores tras lanzarlo al suelo (a veces atraviesa a los jugadores y ellos mismos tienen que pasar por encima para recogerlo), T pose de personajes u otras entidades en momentos determinados. 

- Las partidas en general son monótonas, solo hay 8 mapas y 3 jefes finales. El sistema del dinero destaca por ser lo más ávaro posible, al completar la ronda la ganancia de dinero es muy justa o deficiente para poder comprar armas, armaduras, herramientas, etc. lo que incrementa significativamente la dificultad del juego por el desbalanceo de puntos de vida que tiene los enemigos y el daño de las armas con las que tienes que sobrevivir sin comprar otras mejores.

- Existe 3 dificultades en el juego: normal, difícil e infernal. Si juegas en difícil, si no juegas con otros jugadores es muy complicado ganar la partida; todos los jefes tienen un daño tan alto que con 2 golpes te pueden tumbar. No he tenido aun el privilegio de probar la dificultad infernal, pues tener el nivel 18 (de 30 máximos) no es suficiente para ganar la partida de forma individual en modo difícil.

- Hay muy pocos jugadores online, muchas partidas juegas solo o, en el mejor de los casos, los jugadores comienzan a unirse una vez comenzada.

En conclusión, no recomiendo comprar este juego por el precio sugerido, le doy 7 euros tal y como está el producto actualmente, le falta muchas actualizaciones, contenido y mejoras de mecánicas para que cumplan las expectativas de un juego de la saga Killing Floor.

review:
I don’t know what’s more broken right now — the game or my patience. Killing Floor 3 is currently suffering from that issue, you know, the one that makes the game borderline unplayable unless you enjoy staring at loading screens, broken systems, or features that clearly weren’t finished before someone yelled “ship it.”

This doesn’t feel like a sequel; it feels like a tech demo that escaped containment. Core mechanics stumble over themselves, basic functionality behaves like it’s held together with duct tape, and whatever is going wrong right now completely kills any momentum or fun the game might have had. Nothing ruins the thrill of surviving waves of enemies like fighting the game itself.

What’s especially impressive is how this issue manages to undermine everything Killing Floor used to be good at. Tight gameplay? Nope. Smooth sessions? Absolutely not. Confidence that your time is being respected? Laughable. Every match feels like a gamble where the house always wins and the player always loses.

And let’s not pretend this is some obscure edge case. This is front-and-center, obvious, and embarrassing. The kind of problem that makes you wonder if anyone actually tested the game under real-world conditions or if the plan was just to let players QA it for free.

Right now, Killing Floor 3 isn’t intense, chaotic fun — it’s frustration wrapped in potential. Maybe someday it’ll be worth revisiting. Today is not that day. Until this issue is fixed, consider this less a game and more a warning.

Verdict: Wait. Or don’t. Your blood pressure will thank you.

I played back when the beta first came out. That experience was...bad.
I bought KF3 when it first came out and refunded it because it was still very much in the same shape as the beta.
Now, I bought it during the xmas sales and I can say Tripwire actually is interested in updating their game and improving it while listening to the playerbase. Is it fun? Yeah it's gotten more fun, more content, and more tweaks to improve QOL. It does kind of look like hot garbage unless you're running max settings, so good for you if you can afford that, and there are a few questionable moments that make you think you're playing an early build (audio issues, crashes, animation glitches).

UPDATE 08/10/26: Just hopped on after the Shadow Hunter update and I have to say there have been a wave of improvements and fixes to put the game in a current playable state that people would actually enjoy playing. I still recommend buying on sale, but they are polishing this game, same as when KF1 & KF2 launched.

Killing floor and Killing Floor 2 had rough starts too. Everyone seems to forget that. This seems to be the roughest start but Tripwire has proven they want to nurture and polish this game. Give it a shot when it's on sale

UPDATE: 08/17
Played around some more and after some more time in-game there are still a number of glaring problems. optimization and crashes still seem pretty common. Grinding is waaaaaay too slow. Let me get to the good stuff without having to sink tons of hours into this thin game. Please respect my time. Lastly, make UI less of a chore to navigate, speed things up please

I can't recommend it at the moment. It's got way too many bugs. TLDR - It's got a strong start, but it falls apart quickly. I'd suggest watching a few let's plays on Youtube first, then wait till it's heavily discounted.

It starts out fine, you go about running your fledgling motel: decorating, furnishing and cleaning the rooms. Subsidising your income with a gas pump and selling the occasional chocolate bar and soda.

However once you start growing (about 8-10 hours in) and become dependant on staff the game utterly falls apart.

The employees are completely useless with the possible exception of the gas pumper:

The cashier - often bugs out and just freezes resulting in an ever growing queue of increasingly furious customers. 

The cleaner - cleans 1 thing at a time and seemingly takes forever to clean anything specific (i.e. the motel rooms)

Warehouse assistant (stocker) - Carries 1 box at a time (as opposed to the player who carries 5) and then slowwwwly moves things from the warehouse to the store. They also completely ignore the fact that large bottles only fit in the large slots and so you forever have large bottles clogging up the warehouse as the buffoon has filled the large spaces in fridges with tiny cans.

The housekeeper - By far the worst. She takes an eternity to ready the rooms, carrying one object at a time, then running back to the warehouse to get a towel, then running back to the room to pick up the dirty sheets. USE THE CART YOU MORON.

Then on top of that the process of hiring out rooms is buggy as well. Say you have 4 rooms, well after you've hired out the fourth you'd think the giant Vacancies/No Vacancies sign you spent $1000 on would stop further people enquiring every minute if you have a spare room. Nope, you have to manually turn off the motel part of the business. Then manually turn it back on again when you have a spare room. Awesome.

Stock management is a nightmare. Especially once you unlock the bus station upgrade. Pricing is a pain too as you can't shift prices up and down with arrow buttons, you have to type in a numerical value for each of the dozens of items. Periodically manually changing it as needed.

In the end I had to stop as it was just painful.

review:
Reviewing this game is tough. I enjoy the game and find the mundane operations of a motel/store/gas station engaging. I keep playing it for that reason, despite the critiques below, but definitely feel a certain sense of discomfort with it.

CODING/DESIGN
The game is unpolished in a number of ways (example: buttons or signs that I assume were placed to rectify an issue, but that do not blend in at all) and there are UI things that bug me (example: lists of items that are not alphabetised or sorted in any sensical manner). Some of the people have weirdly proportioned bodies.

DEPICTION OF WOMEN
This very much comes across as a game created by white, hetero men in their early 20s. Is that actually the case? Who knows. The number of women scantily dressed is irritating, as is the specific attention it took to animate some women's skirts blowing up with the breeze a la Marilyn Monroe. Some of the women also sport a sashaying strut that is irritating.
I deactivated it immediately, so I don't know how it actually plays out in the game, but my impression is that the dead bodies in the rooms are often/usually prostitutes. I'm not real keen on the dehumanisation of a vulnerable population. 

ESTHETIC
I think that a lot of my critiques can be summed up by saying that the esthetic rubs me the wrong way. I get that the developers were going for a certain vibe and obviously that is a pretty subjective thing, but the presence of dead bodies, only dirty cops, and robberies that can only be solved with a shot gun just aren't things that I find fun or entertaining. Again, I totally get that for some folks those elements are pluses rather than minuses. I am grateful that those elements can be turned off.

review:
This game is very unpolished, lacks depth, and seems like a money grab. Labels are clumped together and look cheap, translations are incorrect all over the place, and some UI elements don't even show up correctly on the medicine. It gets repetitive within 20 minutes, I highly recommend you DO NOT buy this game. Not now and probably not even in a year. When asking customers what they want, you're given the same options EVERY single time, either: "don't have it" or "sure". 

The graphics are good but that's the only thing I can compliment in the hour I played it. You put a shelf up, order some medicine, put the medicine on the shelf, and proceed to serve a line of 4 customers the entire 40 minute long day - doing the same thing over and over again. When I first unlocked the scale I got excited, only to learn that the customers will use it, get in line, and that's literally it. The progression system is based on every other one - which is - licenses. There's plenty of things to sell, but the game lacks any difficulty, purpose, satisfaction, and everything else a game needs to be successful. 

Not to mention some of the unlocks saying "Available Outside of Demo", what a terrible game. 

This game needs an immense amount of gameplay, polishing, and an entire re-haul before it's worth even a dollar.

review:
Can't recommend in current state. I really want to like this one, but I think there's still a long way to go.

Enjoyed the tutorial for the most part, but after the initial quests it gets *really* repetitive, and leveling takes a really long time. It would take serving over a hundred customers to get to Level 10 to take the first exam to get new meds. There doesn't seem to be an overt way to make more XP by doing well, so having streamlined stock management, good decor etc isn't going to make a difference. I wanted to make it to the first exam and I just got so bored very quickly.

The game is very unpolished too - dialogue translations into English are not very good, and the UI for the different stores is really simplistic and isn't fantastic design-wise. I think there's a LOT of room to improve here by adding more dialogue and bringing in someone who can design the storefronts to be a bit more high-end and professional looking.

There's so much potential here, so hopefully throughout the game's early access period there will be further improvements. At this point I don't feel like I got my money's worth quite yet.

review:
I'm very easily entertained by simulator games, even if most of them are the same. I can find enjoyment in them even if they aren't perfect or have some issues but this simulator has some MAJOR issues. Just glancing at the discussion board will tell you that. 

Game is extremely slow, especially at the start. Milestones are easy to reach and feel rewarding but a lot of the interface is confusing and unclear. You're charged sales taxes every day but can never know ahead of time how much the deduction is. There is a significant game breaking issue around level 20-25 with the unlock of the 5 tier pharmacy shelf where you cannot move product between shelves even if the product is the same. This made restocking a pretty major hassle for me. Many other players are reporting this same issue. 

Amount in stock also reflects products still in boxes but not on the shelf which makes restocking confusing. In order to hire an employee your counter has to be closed and reset for the next day - things that aren't mentioned. The amount of product you can buy vs the size of the shelves is also strange. Why 10 items per box but 20 spaces per shelf? 

Will edit review if bugs are fixed. Might be worth the reduced price but certainly not more.
