review:
I personally like these kind of cozy game, merchant, pawn shop owner and the stories that comes with it
But Trash goblin is missing one important element in ever game, purpose and opposition in the game loop.
the cleaning element is a good start as a time sink because no one wants a dirty item and they sell for less.
but the chiseling is pointless, you will get unlimited mysterious bag after finishing the previous item, but you only get one and is forced to chisels it to find what is inside till you get the next one. 
you can somewhat make out what item it is when you get it but you have no choice to discard it, you are forced to finish the chiseling game to proceed. 
Since customers want specific item, the chiseling game is equivalent of a forced spam left click till you get the right item. There is no multiple mysterious bag with slightly different weight or size to choose from or a bucket of trash for the goblin to rummage through to pick up different mysterious bags, this is no player choice even for cozy game. 
Plus the chiseling game is pointless, there is on negative effect of any kind for spamming left click or repeatedly hitting the buried item, thus this is the equivalent of a "force" lock pick mini game with infinite lock picks and time, no one like this. 
I would suggest since there is no true time limit (this part I love, all cozy game should have this feature) make that if we hit the buried item too many time we break it or break part of it. 
this would be good feature since the best part of trash goblin is the upscale tool, make your creativity go wild and make funny items. plus if you are really lazy this could be a way of discarding mysterious bag or unwanted items. 

Another thing, since you have infinite mysterious bag and time there is no point of making a haggle system (deal or no deal  option). Trash goblin is the same as zero cost business, meaning any thing you sell will only make profit, there is no point of a haggle system that way since there is no point of making big gold in short amount of time. If you want to have one, make it meaning full and have a purpose like it impact reputation or other stuff. 

lastly this could be just my systems problem, but if you use a finger as a the mouse icon make sure the click point is precisely on the edge of the icon not on the finger tip, plus the "click" icon will shift just slightly to cause constant mis-click
I was stuck at the menu for 5-10 min just because i keep mis-clicking stuff. 

Since I am writing this review with around 1-2 hrs of play time, Most of my complains of missing features maybe will show up later in the game, but if so the devs need adjust the progression system, because with my current play time i have already decided to not invest my time into this game anymore, if there is a good feature """"DO NOT"""" leave it at the end, most players will only play 1-2hr to decide should i refund or put it in the infinite growing back log of game they have.

I really love the up scaling tool it is so fun, but i hate the chisel

review:
A [meh] cozy game. It has a very interesting concept, a lot of cool mechanics, customization for the workspace that provides QOL, all of it keeps up the overall interest in earning money. However, the core mechanics are, honestly, simply boring and repetitive. It does have some automation, but not enough.

On the good side. The workspace is neat, you manage space, upgrade it for QOL, add a bit of automation, unlock features, and even customize it. Making money from piecing trash together into a nice or absolutely hideous item is a great concept.

The major issue is chiseling, the core of the gameplay, and it's the same simplistic, repetitive "block-game". Upgrades sped up the process, but it is still tedious. Perhaps splitting them in tiers, as you uncover more and more items from that tier, you'd get a few of them per day without having to chisel.  Honestly, I have no idea how to improve it. This is just the biggest reason for getting bored with the game. For instance, the cleaning is also repetitive, yet you are at least cleaning the item, not generic blocks.

The other personal negative is a constant and overwhelming amount of yapping dialogue from special NPC requests. It's just too much. All I want is to work on trash, make it nice, sell it, maybe go for special requests. But the game felt like a barrage of "special" requests.

There was also a minor pacing issue; the tool upgrades came in too late, and the first hour felt awkward.

review:
I'm truly upset that I can't recommend this game, but I really can't. On paper, this is right up my alley. A shop management game where you find, clean, repair, and sell trinkets to fantasy world customers? Sign me up!

But in practice, the game just doesn't have any depth. Rather than having to go out and dig or hunt for artifacts, they're just randomly handed to you from a bottomless bag one at a time. Then you have to painstakingly chisel them out of a bland, repetitive block breaking game. Then you clean them in a much less fun version of Power Wash Simulator. Then you might combine them with another item.

One of the worst things about this game is that after all that, you just kind of hand it to the customer. No haggling or anything. There's no sense of urgency or fail state, so it really doesn't even matter how much money you get from them. Upgrading tools hardly feels worth it, and the game as a whole seems to lack purpose.

Now for some, the lack of a failure state might be a good thing. Some people might just find this experience zen and relaxing, which is fine. But for me, I need that extra layer of crunch where all the mechanics feed into each other and draw me in. I don't need the game to be difficult or anything, but I need some sense of urgency driving me forward.

Technically I don't even need the failure state. Potion Craft didn't have a failure state, but it did have an extremely deep and complex potion brewing system. Trash Goblin just doesn't have anything like that.

In my 50 minutes I played before requesting a refund I did detect some decent writing, though not much of an overarching story, which is also disappointing. I did like the colorful artwork and the art design though. Good work there.

Some people will fall in love with this in spite of its shortcomings, but that can't be me. still, I can tell the developer put a lot of love and care into this title. I hope it does well and they can come back with something stronger next time.

review:
Gameplay-wise? Fantastic. Tight loop, cute visuals (besides the visual affront that is Aimon), all around enjoyable. But that character—Aimon—kept pulling me out of the experience. Not through any one big “look at me” moment, but through a steady stream of small, curated signals that made it clear: identity was the focus, not character.

As a gay male, "queerness," itself is not a problem however, Aimon’s design walks a very specific line—bald head, heavy makeup, exaggerated features, manly voice cues. Fine, whatever. But then the game goes out of its way to reinforce they/them pronouns, swaps their name mid-dialogue (for totally necessary to the plot and not an attempt to consolidate an agenda) disguise scenes, and toggles between aliases with gender-coded hints that feel more ideological than narrative.

None of it is loud—but if you’re not in a "gender is personality" echo chamber, it’s obvious what’s happening. It’s not representation; it’s identity performance. And it undercuts what could’ve been a genuinely interesting character. Refunded, not because the game isn't fun (it genuinely is), but because this games originality is contrasted by the originality of a repeatedly forced agenda.

review:
No wonder 76 publishers refused to pick up this game.

There were a few warning signs during the window where refunds are possible that this might be a bad game. But business and collecting games are among the genres I like, and it was a cute goblin character to play, and all the people complaining in reviews that I had scanned had done so after barely an hour of gameplay (or during EA when many features were missing)- so I decided to bite the bullet and keep playing to get the full experience and hope for the best as the game found its footing, especially because a couple of the opening scenarios for "regular" customer's requests were actually cute.

Let me tell you- it only gets worse. Much, much worse.

It becomes apparent that the "strangers" customers aren't a huge collection of individually coherent designs being recycled; they're apparently fragmented assets that an rng mixes together and recolors- base face shape, eyes, mouth, hair on head, facial hair, bodies, scars, etc. And, frankly, most all the individual assets are kinda ugly on their own; but when the Frankenstein rng spits out bearded ladies whose mustache doesn't fit their face and is floating in front of their nose, with double chins clipping into their monk tunic, and scar clipping into the bangs drooping down- you really begin to cringe and not want to see anymore.

I bought the delver axe upgrade in the mid-game, it mentioned there was some sort of gameplay with wiggly bags that was supposed to be unlocked- but nothing new happened in the seven hours that remained in my playthrough. Upgrades to chisels and sponges barely shave some time off the minigames once they're fully upgraded, and the special cluster chisel is all but useless thanks to the over usage of purple 1-sided blocks that block it being effective in pokes. There's also still lingering visual glitches, like the rustic teapot having an unbreakable artifact square that's grey, instead of the usual brown. Or items having collision glitches and flying across the store (though those are usually returned to your storage, if there's room, or end up on the worktable the next day when things reset.) Buying the display table helps get nicer items sold at better prices to finance you and auntie's upgrades to satisfy story requirements; when customers aren't coming up and saying they like the look of one item in the product only and want you to tear it apart to give that item, and then you lose not only the cost of the other items that could be sold with it, but also the display boost for that singular item as well. telling picky customers like that to keep moving is your best bet, in a few time cycles someone else will come along and buy as is at premium price.

Also, Aimon, your boss. is a terrible person. Full stop. They are terrible and never redeem themselves. There's a few tidbits of things they supposedly did in the past for you that makes your character and your auntie care about them- but we see NONE of that on screen, And to get one of those tidbits, you have to buy a shop bell, only for the dialogue to then say that it was always yours, your first toy that was gifted by Aimon. Why did I have to pay for my own "toy" to be returned? Oh yes, because Aimon is a terrible person. They are a blackmarket dealer who trades in cursed items, an addict, a rampant criminal who seems to know all the criminals in the city, with zero regard for you- the apprentice they took in at infancy because your auntie needed someone to watch you while she works in dangerous places, and has subsequently groomed to be an unquestioning accomplice to their criminal activity and be a frequent source of exploited labor and funds via your attempts at a legitimate business.

And you are forced to be nice to Aimon every step of the way. You can't refuse their requests as the plot gets progressively more dark with them trying to release a lich and needing you to make illegal sales, hire people to pilfer city museums. Items that are clearly evil in nature, including a trinket that contains numerous humans' soul energy that was drained by a mediocre actor they went to watch. They will also steal those items, like the addict personality that they are, right out of your pockets once obtained because you didn't cough them up as quick as they felt entitled to, then take off with them. Your Auntie spends half the game ignoring concerns you might try to raise, and then decides trying to save someone like aimon is more important than getting her own family to safety and reporting all this, and you have to vehemently agree that aimon is definitely more important. No dialogue choices allowed for the main plot beats, it's on the rails.

Speaking of dialogue choices- when you are given options for dialogue, it's obvious the script doesn't care what you click because the NPCs will answer in a single way for whatever the devs' preferred response clearly was, such as answering questions you never asked, and then continues on with their short monologues, no matter how jarring the disconnect in responses might be because they didn't even bother to add in a single sentence to bridge the responses.

By the end of the game, you've implicated yourself many times as an accomplice to the frog law keeper who is well within her rights to be trying to nail Aimon for everything they've been doing, and you're never given any options but to try covering for aimon. Including saying the massive fog of evil energy coming from behind you in aimon's area, with glowing blue skulls zipping around you like little demonic meteors, is just a glow worm infestation. It's not even believable excuses by a child's standards. But Aimon is lowkey the main character that all other characters must jump on grenades to protect. 

Despite hinting that the lich is a Big Bad, a la D&D standards, that could take out the whole city- the climax is resolved in mere minutes. No aid from you, or specialized forces called in to help out- such as some of your mercenary regular clients you pleased. Nope. Just elderly obese auntie going up with her axe and smacking and/or "suplexing" it into the afterlife- her words, paraphrased. That's all this great evil needed to be defeated. uh huh. Mushroom dude she was with is now disposing of some of the evidence by eating the broken armoire the lich was attached to. 

And the law frog shows up again after auntie leaves, furious that you darn criminals somehow managed to hide all damning evidence, despite obvious signs of crime and the whole block hearing the fight. It makes no sense on such an overlapping timeline for her to get no real evidence, but that's what we're told to swallow for a story ending.

Then the city mayor shows up for the first time and, despite knowing all the bad things that have happened, waves it all away and gives people some presents for ending the threat that they were the ones to unleash in the first place. Because the moral is that crime and anarchy and selfish behavior pays. (I'll also note that while the map for travelling on market days looks like it has a ton of space for new locations to go, there's only two hotspots that ever show up to have a brief reprieve from your living/work cell you're basically imprisoned in.) 

Aimon wakes up from their involuntary nap that auntie sent them to, says a very brief by-the-numbers sorry, and announces they're going on vacation to gently recover. You can watch the store. You are super supportive of them, once again never getting to confront them about the evil stuff or the danger they put you in. 

This is horrible writing from start to finish, with below mediocre gameplay in between that severely stretches out what little plot there is to make it seem like there's more of a game than there actually is.

The end effect is you are connecting who cares to whatever and hoping despite the comminality of who cares and whatever, that RNG won't just roll snake eyes; at least until you remember that it doesn't matter because all you are gonna get is some money to buy more shelf space for ???? who cares.

Just anything to make a shake up to the monotony of cleaning the same 200 things forever with no challenge or even effort beyond bracing your own sanity knowing it will never end, there is nothing else.

I held off on saying avoid this title to check their rate of update. But it barely updates and the updates are of no consequence. It seems apparent they view this as a finished product (doubly so at it's 1.2 version) so as this is what it is, which feels like a premise for a mini game in a rpg that was never finished and never had the game part added. Avoid this title, there are hundreds of better zen games.

review: Got on sale for $2 bucks.  I've gotten $2 worth of enjoyment out of it the game.  Game hangs or crashes when going from home screen to in-world.  Inventory is fairly easy to manage but there's not a lot of info about what size hooks to use for what fish, what reels are compatible with what rods, what rods are good for what type of bait/lures.  It's a bit complicated and assumes the player already know a lot about fishing.  Graphics are just ok.  Pretty scenery but doesn't look very realistic and natural.  Very "cartoony" for lack of a better term.  Gameplay is mostly easy.  Aquariums and trophies are a nice feature but I hate the layout of them, it's a bit over-the-top.  Tons of places for trophies, but I think it's a bit overkill how it is laid out.  As far as gameplay, it's insanely grindy.  Fortunately it's fairly easy to catch fish, and thank god they added a sandbox mode so you can play without the money aspect.  That's a great feature.  Underwater cam is pretty useless. Anyway.  Game needs a lot of work and bug fixes.  It's playable now mostly but the performance is kind of lousy, especially when every time you load in-world there's a 50/50 chance of crashing.  Uninstalled for now but will keep an eye on development and bug fixes.

review:
If you enjoyed Ultimate Fishing Simulator 1... This is not the game for you. UFS2 is a massive step backwards from the first game. The thing that drew me in was being able to see your friends in multiplayer, which the first just did not have (you ain't fooling no one, that big floating bubble your friends appear as is an insult!) HOWEVER, that's the ONLY thing UFS2 has over UFS1.

Outside of that, its a downgrade in visuals, a downgrade in fishing, a downgrade in effects. There's no ripples on the water, from your line or the fish. And half the time when I hooked a fish, they shot out of the lake and got stuck in the ground anyway...the rest of the time, the fish casually swam towards me in the air.

Screen-space reflections provided by the Unity engine are a huge no-no in a fishing game, as the lake constantly has your rod and hands grossly reflected over the top of everything. It looks ugly, the devs put ZERO effort in here, and it really shows.

I get that the game is early access, so will I refund? Possibly not... but they have a long way to go before UFS2 is even close to the standard of UFS1.

Can not recommend. Not even worth the $2.50 on sale.

Man..spending almost 45 minutes trying to catch a catfish that was literally close enough for me to pick it up when it took the bait is infuriating.
I was using a level 10 Rod, level 12 reel, level 10 line and a spinning lure in Kiel Canal and the fish never seem to get tired.
The fish shot to 2000 ft out, gave me 200 ft, then shot up to 3000, gave me another 200, then shot up to 5000 ft out and was going from 5000 to 4700 and would never seem to get tired. I fought with this thing for 45 minutes and it never got tired...ever. There's no way that a 70-80 pound catfish has a 2nd and 3rd wind like that. That's just insane. I found myself nodding off in the middle of trying to reel it in because of how long it was taking. I got tired before the fish did. I ended up having to just give up and go to bed.

 I can't recommend this game until the developers or "developer." figure out a better system for tiring fish out. It should not be 100% reliant on the equipment, if you fight a fish for 45 minutes, at no point after the 30 minute mark should the fish have enough energy to keep pulling your line to the other end of the map with no return. I understand that the "fight" is exciting, but most of the time it's just the fish winning and the players giving up because it's too much of a hassle.

Positives -I like the environments and levels and choices for equipment and the graphics are really quite good, just need a better system for fighting fish.

Played this game for a long time and went all the way through every map. 

The positives first: 
1) Fish hook pretty quickly. 2) Maps are diverse and so are fish. 3) Error 404 additional reasons not found.

On to the bad stuff: 

1) Fish are VERY difficult to catch. Not the small stuff, those are fun and challenging. I fought a shark for an hour. 1 hour of my life before he swam all the way to the end of my line and I got fed up, turned my trim to 100% and broke him off.

4) Your house has a massive aquarium you can't use. Fish can only go in the aquarium if they're under 30 lbs or so, which is very few, and there's a HUGE aquarium taking up the center of your house that you can't put anything in. 

TLDR: I don't regret getting the game, I'm glad I only paid $7. If it's ever actually finished I'll amend this review. I did have fun, only because I played with a friend.

Teal Deer- I found the game to be more shallow and repetitive then many games in the simulator genre. It also felt more like an early access game especially at the $20 price point. Loading times can feel like the game froze at times, and the mouse acceleration feels way too high. If I keep the game I will update my review as it gets updates as it has only been out a couple of days at this point.

I am really on the fence about this game. First if you are planning on picking it up and using the 2 hours to see if you like it that isn't going to work. The tutorial explains mechanics that while not difficult won't be intuitive so I don't recommend just skipping what it is specifically asking you to do especially since you are on tracks until those specific tasks are finished. 90 minutes in and I have picked up and sold 2 cars. I can see this tutorial being like Skyrim where on multiple playthroughs you just want to skip it or speedrun it. But it is good for walking you through what you will need to do. That said you should take advantage of the demo or YouTube to see if it is something you're interested in.

I am leaning towards the no on a recommendation because at $20 for a fully released non-early access game there are some some things that need to be optimized, and the beginning of the game feels really shallow. With 2 cars I have unlocked car washes (soap up and rinse off), scrape off rust, apply putty, sand down putty, and paint. They all have the same mechanics. Use specific tool from radial menu. Press X to scan car and highlight everywhere you need to use the tool (60-100% of the car so far). Use the mouse to slowly go over every inch of the highlighted area. Then switch tool and do the same. That is 6 mechanics that mostly makes you go over all of the car the exact same way. Next there is the use the magic scanner. See what is in red and decide if you want to "repair it". That involved choosing a specific part spraying it with a magic juice that suddenly made a giant hole appear and applying tape to it. The spraying part is the exact same as all the other mechanics previously described!

I am someone who enjoyed house flippers, Spray Wash Simulator and car mechanics simulator. This feels more shallow then all of those

review:
I really wanted to like this game as I enjoyed Gas Station Simulator (albeit with some reservations)

Positives:

The repair and bodywork mechanics are different from what you might have seen before, for the first few repairs it is interesting.

The town is large enough that exploring is possible

Negatives:

The bartering system is pointless and frustrating. If you put a car up for 5500 and someone offers you 3500 you should be allowed to chase them away with a baseball bat. The fact that you have to massively over-price your cars to get anywhere close to market value is stupid.

The random vandal turning up is equally as pointless and annoying as Dennis from Gas Station simulator. It serves no purpose other than to be a pain in the arse.

99.9% of the environment is for decoration only. At least in GSS you can clean up a reasonable amount of the junk, in this game you can't pick anything up, you just have to tolerate the piles of trash everywhere.

Mesh clipping. Maybe because I'm a dev I notice this more than most but it's a pet peeve as it shows a lack of care went into the design, tyres clipping through road surfaces, trash meshes embedded in each other, it's just shoddy workmanship.

Poor audio design. The narrator voice is muffled and the balance of the effects is not very well thought out.

Repetitive. Basically, once you've done one or two repairs, or washes it gets old really quickly. It starts to feel grindy and uninteresting whilst you're still in the early stages of the game. Things don't improve much from then on.

More parts for the vehicles

Brand-specific or generation-specific components

A larger map would help a lot – sometimes I wonder where all the cars are coming from when I’ve bought 10 of them from the same NPC.

Maybe even create multiple maps, so you could drive between towns and check out new car markets?

I’d also love to see toolsets unlocked over time, where you go out and purchase specific machines to upgrade your workshop. Right now, upgrading the office and work areas is mostly just visual – you clean up, expand, and make room for more tools.

review:
The game starts off promising, but it quickly turns into an exhausting grind with no real sense of progression.

Even after hiring employees, you're still doing 90% of the work yourself. Their presence barely improves efficiency — for example, to wash a car, you still have to drive it to the wash bay, assign the employee, and then wait 2–3 real-time minutes for them to finish. The same goes for every step of the process: you must meet with the seller, buy the car, personally drive it to the mechanic (who only works if you already have the needed parts), then wait another 3 minutes for repairs. Then it's off to the body shop for another 3-minute rust removal and repaint job, followed by the car wash again, then the photo booth, and finally to the sales area. After all that, you still need to go into the office and manually register the car for sale.

None of this can be automated or delegated, and every single vehicle goes through this same drawn-out routine. Meanwhile, once the store is open, you can sell 5 cars in under 5 minutes — meaning your lot is constantly empty because prepping even one car is such a time sink.

This game feels like busywork disguised as simulation. There's no real management here — just repetitive manual labor, stretched out by timers. It’s more tedious than fun.

If you’re like me and enjoy simulator games, trust me — there are better options out there.

review:
This is another of those games that deserves a 'Mixed' review, rather than a positive or negative. It's a game that whilst fun at first, does quickly fall into the mundane repetitiveness that many of these "Simulator" type games seem to follow.
Lets go through what the game does well first;
- Fun game play and basic to understand
- Graphics are okay, standard for this type of generic 'simulator' titled game
- Consistent updates from the dev's and they are adding new content into the game as per the dev log's. 
- Is quite a fun game for the first 10 hours or so, this does wear down in line with the repetitiveness of the game play but is interesting to start
- Game concept is fun, I like the idea of being able to run my own car dealership and build on that existing foundation to a bigger company
- The amount of jobs you can do is quite a nice variety (I.E. Mechanical, bodywork, washing etc.) this is quite a nice concept which at first does keep you quite busy in the game.

Now, the not so good;
- The game play, whilst interesting at first, does become incredibly tedious with the player having to repeat the same 4/5 jobs for each car. Washing cars becomes tedious fast as there is no variety to the amount of dirt / rust / damage to individual vehicles, with most of them having a preset amount of both which every car follows.
- Car selection is very limited and basic, with the core element of the game revolving around the buying and selling of cars, shouldn't this be a high priority for variety?
- Working on the cars is very primitive and lacks detail. Whilst this isn't the core element of the game, if they are implementing this as the main route to make more profit on your vehicles, shouldn't this be more interactive rather than just the same repetitive part disassembly routine
- Its too easy. There are no mistakes to be made, selling dodgy cars doesn't have any effect on your dealerships reputation, and its impossible to lose money on a car unless you purposely sell it cheap. Doesn't really give the game much depth in terms of difficulty and makes the act of making profit on cars seem less rewarding.
- Lack of dealership upgrades cosmetically. Whilst I understand this game is all about being the Tom Skinner of car sales, why does it have to look quite so shit? Can't we at least spend our "Hard earned" cash on making the place look a little nicer. The whole thing just feels unfinished and a bit rough because of it, and really limits the progression for the player.
- Inventory size. Why is my inventory so small that I can only hold a very limited amount of parts at one time. When you are consistently repairing cars you do have a lot of junk parts build up in your inventory, which quickly becomes a pain when buying / selling additional parts.
- Lack of story line / progression. Whilst the game does try to implement a feeling of a story line into the game, it is incredibly weak and menial, and after level 7 reputation is reached, really means sweet FA in the long run. This makes it quite hard to see a progressive element in continuing to buy / sell cars, and removes any sense of objective from the game.
- There's something about this game that just feels very unfinished. I'm not sure if its the total lack of depth / progression / detail in the game, but it just doesn't feel like a well made game. It is very in-line with the current trend of releasing simulator titles with bog standard assets and low grade production quality, whilst the game is fun to play, it just doesn't stand alone in the simulator category as one of the better games.

Conclusion;
Overall, I'd give this game a "Meh", its not good, its not bad, it's just "Meh". Is it worth the £17.99 in the steam store? Absolutely not. Should you give it a go if its on sale for -50%? Yes. But at this price, and this lack of depth / detail, its really not a game I can recommend. If you are looking for a game that has a far deeper mechanical / sales / progressive element to it, go for car mechanic simulator 21', its a much better game at a much fairer price. Whilst I look forward to the future updates to the game and seeing what the dev's can add, for now my opinion would be not to buy Car dealer simulator until the glaring issues with the games have been addressed.

review:
Im absolutely gutted to write a bad review for this game, because it has the world of potential under its feet. I thought it was an early access title, then realised it wasn't and I was playing a final product (Albeit with updates incoming but not the point).

First, why its SO GOOD:

- Addictive.
- Finding a bargain and making money gib dopamine
- Felt like genuine progression for the first few levels with huge progression on the horizon....

....But its at a few levels in you realise, that what you have been doing, is pretty much it for the entire game. Buy a car, do it up (Or have one of your mechanics do it), sell it for profit. Rinse, repeat. There isn't a game beyond a certain point.

Also - Fuel Station at home? a 100+ car park? Who the heck needed those? You sell cars the same day you put them on sale, and you are individually responsible for moving them around. Imagine if you had 100 cars to run around to each and every station!?

You can buy a Tow Truck and its upgrade for $60k which makes picking up cars only 10% easier as you can carry two, but you can't pickup two large ones, so negates the point completely. Furthermore, you can tow large vehicles with the base standard trailer hitch you get.

I found car sales pricing to be extremely patchy. I would buy one "Porsche" and make it perfect, sell for £60k, the next for £80k, even though the mileage and year were extremely similar. Sometimes I would get random beaters that fetched in immense cash, and others that weren't worth the hassle, but figuring it out was actually very difficult.

Automation would be nice here - Create a production line eventually where you can oversee it, what comes in (Quality vs Quantity), oversee pricing vs competition and the market, etc.

I really wish the devs the best because this is a cracking effort, but getting to this point in just a short few days has left me gutted.

review:
Car Dealer Simulator looks gorgeous and starts strong: the one‑man, used‑car hustle feels right and the early restoration loop makes sense. But the game quickly funnels you down a single path and the late game turns hollow. Selling is trivial—lots clear in seconds even above market—and there’s no real demand, negotiation, or sales floor energy. Staff are static and micro‑managed, with teleporting behaviors and no actual salespeople, while customers pop in and out without a buying journey. The experience tilts oddly toward tow‑truck logistics, culminating in the seven‑vehicle hauler as the marquee upgrade instead of land, showrooms, or operational depth—so you never truly feel like you’re managing a dealership.

What’s missing are the pillars of the business: building placement and lot planning; trade‑ins with appraisal/reconditioning; financing and F&I; new‑vehicle ordering delivered to the lot (lower margins, higher volume for late‑game pacing); accessories and service/parts; and role‑based staff with skills in sales, finance, and tech work. Layer in market conditions and customer intent (shoppers seeking specific vehicles), price elasticity, and inventory that doesn’t evaporate instantly, and the sim could blossom. As it stands, it’s a beautiful shell that misses the mark on dealership management.

I wasn't sure whether or not to leave a review for this one as I was a bit mixed but ultimately feel like for the price I can't recommend it currently.

Technically wise it could use some optimisation, running on medium settings with frame gen + DLS activated and I'm still getting some random stutters here and there (5600X with a 4070 TI Super).

Voice acting seemed off for me, in the sense that some lines just felt robotic and not spoken like a human. I noticed that AI was used for translations so perhaps this has something to do with it? This jarring voice acting was coupled with some weird animations, most notably for me is the sprinting animation in third person which for lack of better way of saying it, looks goofy.

Combat was okay, it played kind of like a generic third person shooter (was considering first person mode but got a warning this was experimental?) and while I'm sure it gets more interesting later the issues I did have made me ultimately put this down and refund for now.

While I understand that jank is par for the course for early access, I expect a certain amount of optimisation and polish when you're charging 30 pounds (while on a launch sale) after having a kickstarter campaign.

Woke up to play it today and was smacked in the face with immediate AI voice acting for NPCs, merchants and even the damn main character in some places..... On top of that I get to the first vendor to offload some items and he has 1,000 money. I didn't go out of my way to farm up loot but the 8-9 items I have to sell him are in total worth about 9,000....... I can't even sell the crap the game randomly awarded me for the little killing/exploring I've done.

I'm not saying this can't be salvaged, but anyone considering making the purchase just WAIT. Let them hopefully patch the game, finish the voice acting or ultimately fall flat on their face as a studio for releasing this hot garbage. I've never been the "Early Access sucks" guy but this is CLEARLY why some people feel that way.

Game had a minor hotfix patch today. A couple promising things, so I went back and played a few more hours to give it a second chance. The AI voicelines become more and more frequent the further I got. Also apparently the "dismantle" skill (alternative to selling your hard earned loot) is only learned from a SCIENTIST faction member, so god help you if you choose to assist the Mercs/Mutants at the start of the game you will be unable to dismantle items for some time until you meet them later in the game. I wish I could say the game is worth buying and supporting right now but its just not.

review:
This game is really weird to me. The first game was really cool and I really enjoyed it. It was a awesome blend of Sci-fi, horror, mystery, exploration and atmosphere. It had RPG elements and base building elements but those werent really the focus. 

Chernobylite 2 however... it's like they removed everything that made the first game so cool and doubled down on all the stuff that wasn't. This feels like a wonky fantasy fallout game or something. The environments look cool, but the gameplay itself is just so boring. The story so far, is just not interesting. 

Collecting loot in games is not exciting for me. The first Chernobylite there was something calming and almost hypnotizing about using the scanner and going and finding the loot you needed. Chernobylite 2 feels like any other RPG loot system. Just kill stuff spam Loot All and have inventory full of random items. Looting was in the first game as well, but it was different. This feels like its way more of a focus. It just feels like a medicore RPG game now instead of this cool scifi / horror story. 

I thought the first game did a good job on balancing the action  and the horror. And there were times when Chernobylite 1 was actuallly pretty scary. Chernobylite 2 is the exact opposite in this regard. It's just mindless run and shoot pack of RPG mobs that have health bars. They even have axes and shields and shit. You can even cast spells its like wtf... Like, Igor passed out in some green gas and is having a fever dream. Thats what this feels like.

review:
Let this intro serve as not just a warning to potential buyers but a message to the developers and also provide some context for my early access review:

Chernobylite was my GOTY for 2021 until Inscryption dropped and stole the gold. Get Even was a fantastic story driven stealth shooter with a really cool gameplay hook as well. The Farm 51 always approach their games with a clear vision and the final result is every time something unique and worthwhile. However, Chernobylite 2 SHOULD ONLY BE PLAYED/PURCHASED by those of you interested in supporting the devs during early access either financially or by playing and providing your own unique feedback. There are just too many issues both technical and gameplay related that will only serve to frustrate players. To sum it up as simply as possible: this game makes a terrible first impression which combined with the Early Access tag can bury a game. Pros and Cons incoming. Cons will include genuine feedback but I will add any additional feedback after the list of cons.

PROS:
- Choice between 1st and 3rd person perspective allows players to choose their preferred method of play 
- Voice acting is nearly on par with previous games from the devs (although some of the dialogue sounds like placeholder AI, which shouldn't be looked at as a con for Early Access, please stop chewing on your keyboard)
- Base building is even better and more expansive than the first game and I can only imagine what a fully decked out base would look like (seriously addicting)
- Melee combat is surprisingly smooth and feels not only functional but a viable way to approach many combat encounters. Although the input queue will definitely trip up some of the button spammers out there (I played in 1st person).
- Worldbuilding is strong and plays off the foundation set by the first game very well.
- Great OST, on par with the first in terms of tone and style. Not sure if it's the same composer as the first game, but there is a reason I bought the OST for the first one and I will buy this one as well if it lives up to that in the end.

CONS
- Tons of graphical issues. You name it and the game probably has it. I don't mind this stuff for Early Access, but it reaches a point where your immersion is just obliterated making it nearly impossible to really stay in the game.
- Some key rebinding doesn't actually work, which combined with inconsistent tutorialization can make it difficult to figure out what some buttons do. Seriously, during the tutorial section when you're trying out the classes (which ends up being basically meaningless when you make your class choice) I thought I was doing something incorrectly because the NPC kept saying I was doing something wrong no matter what I did during the encounter which made me second guess how the weapons actually worked.
- Deeper distinction between classes (which may or may not come later in the game). The RPG choices presented to certain classes don't seem very interesting or intuitive. And it looks like any class can use basically any gear with no penalty? 
- There is very little feedback for anything that you do outside of swinging a melee weapon. I didn't even know I leveled until I got back to the base because there is no sound or music or fanfare whatsoever. For how absurdly overbearing the UI can be, the fact that it didn't tell me I had leveled in any meaningful way just felt so strange.
- Speaking of UI, somehow the building elements from the first game (building stations like healing, ammo crafting, etc.) were made more difficult because of how little of your screen you can actually utilize when placing a station. If there is a button to minimize or remove UI during that process I didn't see it (and I'm willing to just be dumb on this one) but the fact that either wasn't obvious, or just set as the default is incredibly frustrating. This was exacerbated further by the incredibly poor lighting in the base itself. I don't mind low lighting when you're out exploring (in the first game especially it made for some incredibly tense moments), but for the building stuff, you should either just have better visibility by default OR the building should just be moved into the base building menu as well. Other than porting over the elements from the first game for the sake of ease, I can't imagine why this wasn't just a change that was made in general.
- This is probably my biggest criticism of the game and I don't think it is necessarily an Early Access issue so please take special noteL The enemy types are far too varied mechanically to look so similar. The ones that shoot look like the ones that swing look like the ones that punch. I don't mind them all looking so similar, it makes sense in the lore and it would be weird to change it too much, but something has to be considered. If you're standing in green grass near trees and a Chernobylite deposit with 4 or 5 Chernohosts that all look identical but you can't tell which one is firing at you while another one swings, that's just not a good approach to enemy design. There are far too many examples of this done right to fail this hard.

I may update my review with additional feedback when there are major changes, but as it stands I may not come back until 1.0 so I can experience the world and story as intended and not with so many issues. I have no doubt whatsoever that the final product can absolutely be one of the best RPGs on Steam. Even in its current state (2 days into Early Access) it is superior to mainstream garbage like Starfield, But I want newcomers to get the best that the team at The Farm 51 are capable of. So in the meantime, I would recommend either replaying OR playing for the first time the original Chernobylite. A fantastic game from fantastic developers and by the time you get through that one, the second one might be in a more acceptable state.

review:
What a shame. The first Chernobylite was a great game. The atmosphere and dark and gritty gameplay made for a nice mix of survival FPS and horror, with a base building element. I have absolutely no idea what would compel the developers to stray so far away from what made the first Chernobylite so great, but here we are. I even replayed the first game in preparation for this one when I saw it was releasing in a couple months only to be extremely disappointed.

The devs changed basically everything about the game for this, and from the very start of the game where you get to test the 3 'classes' it feels like an awfully made futuristic ubisoft shovelware clone. It's truly unbelievable as I loved the first game and was really looking forward to this one, but from what I can see, this game takes almost nothing from the first game, which wouldn't be an issue if the game was halfway decent.
	
There are now 6 classes, which specialize in melee, firearms, and chernobylite(magic), or a mix of the 3. They also changed the combat system to one that IMO resembles a mix of skyrim and a wannabe dark souls. Basically braindead AI that spam attacks you and you can block or dodge. Obviously the hitboxes are pretty bad and the game is sadly easy even on hard difficulty because you can just spam dodge and during the dodge animation you're unable to get hit, even if the shot goes straight through you. The NPCs and ESPECIALLY the player model look absolutely horrendus, they literally look and move like aliens who are pretending to be humans. It also seems like they picked and chose what lines would be voice acted by your character and others. I was 5 hours into the game and my character started talking in an unmistakably AI generated voice, and then 5 minutes later his normal voice comes back. Oh, and the game runs like absolute garbage even at the lowest settings and looks like garbage even at 'cinematic' settings.

If you enjoyed the first game and are looking for more of that, or even if you haven't played the first game, please just look at some gameplay videos, specifically of the combat, and you will see the vision that they have for this. It's a joke what they turned this game into. If you are looking for more of the first game, unfortunately this ain't it. 

To be completely honest even if the game looked good and ran well, I would still be extremely disappointed because this is such a jarring change from the first game that I'm surprised that they wouldn't just make a new title to ruin. RIP Chernobylite.

review:
Extremely upset with the state of this game. It is in no way ready for even early release. This is a $40 beta test. Cool premise, good graphics when they don't glitch out, poor optimization, and just overflowing with bugs. Add to your wishlist and follow but DO NOT PURCHASE at this time!

I don't usually post a negative review but this is horrible...especially since I decided to do a couple of the rifts tonight and did not earn ANYTHING! None of my loot, none of my exp, absolutely zero benefit. 

Highly disappointed to this point. 


RE:BUGS BUGS BUGS
Doesn't look bad, but this is definitely rushed to release.

1. Loot and other objects fall through the ground. This especially occurs in the port area on the sandy areas, when crossing bridges and over tunnels, and when there is an underground facility below where you are fighting or scanning.

2. When going through portals, your clothing glitches over your face and head making first person untenable to proceed. The only way to correct is to force a new loading. Unfortunately this is happening often in the "Breach" portion of the game that does not allow saving and reloading. Had to quit the game and start over multiple times. Very annoying.

3. Storage is extremely limited early on. Either storage needs to be increased or the scrapping of items needs to be available very very early.

4. When placing benches a "snap to" option with a grid would be nice...please!

5. Melee combat is ridiculously buggy...you can be in a fight and swing until you stamina is gone and get zero hits...but the enemy can be swinging all over the place and nearly kill you with 1 hit.

6. EXP gain needs to be worked on. After 5 days in game, following the story and doing a little exploring but not much, only enough experience to gain two stat points. This is much to slow for how quickly the enemy and gear requirements climb.

7. Goes along with #6 but the amount of locked areas that you will have to try and remember to come back to and pick up what every is behind the door you need 12 strength or the crystals that need 15 psyche to get past etc.etc. is really really annoying. I don't want to have to revisit every single place I went to following the story just to see if these crates have anything useful in them. And when they don't have useful items for my current level whenever I get enough points to actually access them people will just not bother.

8. REALLY REALLY should use the same voice on characters...following the story, get immersed, and then the same dialog with the same character suddenly has a different voice...way to break the story telling.

Probably more things as I continue playing but wanted to start a list...I'll keep adding here.

I'm disappointed to have given this game a thumbs down. I loved Chernobylite 1. I bought it in EA, and played it throughout each and every update, and i love the game now. I saw they were making a second one, i was excited, and bought it in EA too. I wish i could say that i was having the same enjoyable time that i did when i played the first one in and throughout EA.

The characters feel soulless. They feel devoid of all emotion. The area that you are put into feels deliberately empty. What i mean by that is, there's no ambience, or no feelings of loneliness, it feels like they just didn't want to put any other characters in, apart from crucial quest characters. I also have to say, i saw people talk about AI voice acting, I'm guessing they were talking about the AI that speaks to you. I have little thoughts on this, i just wish they used actual voice actors and not a text-to-speech program.

The optimisation needs so much work. My i9-9900k, 3060 and 32gb runs on medium and i get 40fps, thats if there are no mobs on screen or any effects. I hate to compare, but MHWilds gives me 55fps on medium and that game is horrifically unoptimised. Please work on the optimisation.

Overall.. whilst its an EA game, it still needed more time to be developed before it even got launched into an EA state. This isn't to say that i won't be keeping an eye on it, look at updates etc., because i really want this game to be successful. A game being in EA shouldn't excuse the state it is in. It's lazy, it's allowing games to be further released without any work done, and it needs to stop.

review:
I do honestly want to like this game. I loved the first game, and was so excited about a sequel that I did back the kickstarter. Chernobylite 2 leaves me......confused.

Overall the game is fine? I love exploring the exclusion zone, I love that Igor is around to guide us......and thats really it. It's not even that the rest of the game is bad. Heck I can see why some enjoy a lot of its elements. But if you want a true sequel to the first game, this really isn't that.

Combat is now souls-like, clearly with the melee combat in mind, but that means gunplay and the, admittedly interesting gauntlets suffer a bit to get it all to work. The slow, methodical combat in from the first game is now just mindlessly blitzing almost anything you see. 

The Main character almost feels like he was originally meant to be a custom voiceless character before getting shoehorned in for a personal story element, but all that does imo is force you to play as the most generic, boring SoB i've seen in a game. The first game had a very personal story for Igor but it was well implemented into the overarching narrative about him finding his wife using information you grab about the Chernobyl Disaster. Generic Man (legit can't remember his name) has a wife, and she's left him for a decent enough reason, and that's all I remember about the guy. I think scrapping a pre made character in favour for a custom one would do wonders for the game. Focus the story on the world you're stuck in without the need for side bits about a very unlikeable MC.

Base Building is fine. Feels a little bare bones right now but I can assume there will be more added and the feature fleshed out in the future. In fact, all my other complaints can be attributed to early access, and I wouldn't normally be too critical about that. I mean I left NMRIH2 a positive review cause it feels good under the EA jank. But the fundamentals built into Chernobylite 2, that probably can't/won't see much change at all, really sour the overall experience for me. 

Maybe in the future I'll look at this game favourably, but right now, I'm left very confused and admittedly a little sour.

I'm spending more time staring at the PDA in the bottom corner of the screen than the world around me. I don't want to play the PDA game. I want to play the amazing Chernobylite game in the amazing Chernobylite world.

PDA map...why doesn't it zoom in and out?

Coming back to the point again: get rid of the PDA. Why do I need it up to scan the world around me? I've got perception, that's my skill, not the PDA's skill. I want to stop looking at the PDA and start looking at the world. Let me scan the world independent of the PDA, highlight or mark the items in the world around me, and then also maybe have them on a smaller zoomable mini map tucked away in the top-right corner of the screen.

When first starting the game the default mouse speed was set extremely slow. Fixed by going into settings.

The first couple of hours playing were visually horrible. Why was everything so close to the POV of the character? Found the field of vision setting, but even at max its still a bit too close.

The character models feel like they're based on late 1990's code and modelling, just up scaled. Not lifelike or fluid.

The voice acting... The voice actors come across like they're reading individual lines into a microphone in a room on their own, not actually speaking dynamically with another person. The dialogue between characters is so...halting. It's not fluid and breaks any sense of immersion. Again, it feels like late 1990's technology.

Text windows on the Build Your Base screen take up way too much space and stick around needlessly. Why can't I zoom in and out? This is a part of the overall problem that is a pattern in the game so far. Too much clutter. Not enough immersion and realism.

After building a room and attempting to place a workbench in that room, the screen is again taken up by way too many things leaving way too little of the screen open to see the room and the item that you're trying to place in it.

Can't leave the Build Your Base screen if you've got a large room selected but not placed due to rocks in the way.  Hit ESC to leave the interface?  You get a popup asking you to ACCEPT or DECLINE the error message preventing you from leaving the interface.  Neither option lets you leave Build Your Base....you just get left with the same unplaced room and stuck in the interface.

Using a workbench: why isn't ESC a default key to exit the workbench screen alongside the displayed odd choice of the TAB key? TAB isn't a game standard choice for exiting screens, if you're going to use it, at least keep ESC as a secondary exit key. ESC should get you out of every single screen that you are in while playing the game.

Same problem with skipping conversation lines of dialogue. Why is ENTER your choice of key bind here? Why are users taking their hand off the mouse to move to the keyboard and hit ENTER? The SPACE key should be default, or at least a secondary key. Left hand is already at the standard WASD home location, that leaves the thumb to readily hit the SPACE key to skid dialogue lines quickly.

Attribute screen: you need to be able to click an attribute to lock it in so you can go down and scroll through the explanation text window. Currently you have to try and carefully weave your mouse pointer around other items to get down to scroll the text window without inadvertently changing it to a different item.

Systems and quests aren't thoroughly tested to be intuitive and error free.  During Night Activities in learning how to build an extractor the steps are clunky and at the end you're audibly prompted to return to the base, but attempting to leave has the stalker appear out of no where saying you can't leave....why?  I dunno, no quest info on the screen, but apparently you need to talk to him before leaving and him automatically stopping you from leaving apparently isn't a good enough time for him to just say what he has to say.  Again, the close camera distance made this quest annoying trying to place pipes or a power line especially with all the things taking up screen space.  Looking at you needless PDA and over-sized quest text that never goes away...

Combat just feels sluggish and awkward. The original game was gritty and realistic and so far the in game experience feels like a child's game for pre-teens for combat. Fights seem...episodic not natural or a part of the world.

In 3rd person, you can strafe while holding down aim for a ranged weapon...but not a melee weapon? Blocking is bound to the right mouse button instead of aiming like with a ranged weapon. A better solution is needed. Normally a modifier like SHIFT or another key would let you strafe, but I haven't found a modifier key to strafe in 3rd person melee....I just wobble around inefficiently trying to line up shots. 3rd person melee is needlessly frustrating. Where is the elegance of the original game?

3rd person combat has none of the gritty realism of the original game. Why? Why was this changed? Melee in first person leaves odd disorientation after multiple swings. Where did the enemy go? Why did my camera angle change?

Getting melee'd through the wall of a cargo container needs to get fixed.

I selected the gun based class. I want to play as a sniper and a gun-based character...but here I am playing a mindless melee character by default due to the limitation of too little ammo and guns just not matching up. I didn't want to play like this, why am I being funnelled into swinging a melee weapon when the game asked me how I wanted to play? Cater the in-game experience to the class chosen by the player.

Typos in the on screen text display of NPC audio conversations need to be fixed. Igor needs to use the word "he'll" not "heill."

Going to the map screen by hitting "M" needs to center the location of the mouse pointer. Currently if you've been turning and then press "M" the map screen will slide all the way to the left or the right until you manually center your mouse in away from the edge of the screen.

I understand you're in EA, but these are really core components that are key to user experience and immersion. Why has the game strayed so far from the original game's design and mechanics? There's a reason that it was successful and fun to play. It feels like the development team may be working with a yes-man culture where everyone is possibly being too polite and not enough honest discussions are being had or encouraged to be brutal on pet code projects or sunken resources into code that is simply not good.

This is not the original Chernobylite game deepened and uplifted into a better version of the first game.  This is a scrapping of the original and a rewrite from the bottom up, having not held true to the original game play experience....which is why users are on this Steam page hoping for more of the same...only better.

review:
Chernobylite 2... So, as a backer for both the original Chernobylite and now its sequel, Chernobylite 2, I was super hyped for this early access release. I even got to play the "pre-launch" version, which actually ran a bit better overall. Honestly, though, that excitement's been a bit tough to hold onto. This review's coming out a bit late because when the game first launched, I just couldn't play it – the performance issues were really rough.

Fast forward almost three months, and while the game is technically playable now, it's still pretty rough around the edges when it comes to performance. It's a real bummer, honestly, because I had such high hopes for it.

Diving into the actual gameplay, it's a bit of a mixed bag. The melee combat feels like it's trying to be a bit like Dark Souls but maybe missed some of the key ingredients, and everything feels really fast-paced. As for gunplay, it's okay, but it just doesn't have that satisfying, weighty feel that made shooting in the first Chernobylite so great.

The classes are decent, though many of them do feel a bit similar. I have to give a huge shoutout to the Chernomancer, though – that one is genuinely unique and a ton of fun! It's basically your magic-user but with all these cool mutant abilities, which is a really fresh idea.

So, even though I haven't been able to sink a ton of hours into it yet, I wanted to share my initial thoughts for anyone considering picking it up. Right now, in its current state, I'd probably suggest holding off for a bit.

The game feels like it's trying too hard to be Elden Ring, when it really should be leaning into a STALKER 2-style experience. I'm hoping for a shift in direction at some point, aiming for more of a shooter RPG vibe, much like STALKER.

However, I really do believe in Farm 51. They've shown a great commitment to their games in the past, and I'm optimistic that they know what they're doing. I have a strong feeling that in about six months or more, this game could really transform into something special. So, if you're interested, I'd highly recommend adding it to your wishlist and checking back on it later in the year.

As a big fan of the STALKER series, this franchise means a lot to me. I'm really looking forward to seeing how Farm 51 continues to develop the game in the coming years, and I'll definitely be updating this review as things progress!

review:
oh I've mixed feelings on this.... but I'm thumbing it up.

For early access it's alright and it shows a lot of promise. I'm not captivated or blown away - but I didn't bounce of it as much as I expected. Performance started out as acceptable with the occasional bottleneck in the open world (I'm assuming the game is loading in assets and might be happier on an SSD?) although it seemed to get worse the further I progressed in the game. 

In terms of story the idea of factions trapped under a Chernobyllite dome duking it out with mutants works for me and I'm easily won over by open worlds. Exploration, surviving and finding your way is fun. Or at least it should be. 

There's a lot here I'm unsure about.  I haven't put a lot of hours into the game - so I may have missed things somewhere. But so far...

There doesn't seem to be a lot to do outside of missions. The original gave you a map with a specific objective (retrieve ammo, meds, whatever) with the option to pick up resources on the way. With a larger map there's the invitation to explore and players need to be rewarded for going off the beaten track. An open world which is just a backdrop to trundle between story missions is wasted. We need to be able to rummage around and discover things for ourselves. Add to that I've come across the occasional scrap between mutants and humans - I'm guessing these are are scripted (which is fine)- but I'd like to discover characters outside the main story somewhere in the Zone (perhaps occasionally giving me something to do which may annoy, or woo, a faction along with a reward). And there's many a building that *looks* interesting from the outside - and that's as far as it goes, because once it you get closer you find the entrances boarded up.

This is a lot more combat heavy. The original impressed that combat was something best to be avoided, or low key and tactical.  This fully embraces slugging it out in melee and firefights, and it's easy to run into a mob of chernobylite riddled mutants and get into a tussle. The inclusion of 'bullet sponge' enemies (thankfully going to be addressed) was a wrong move and contributed to much frustration in the early game - having to take one down for things to open up. There is a tension... I miss the slower pace of the original where you felt vulnerable in the face of opposition. EZ throws plenty of mutants at you, but then the game starts to feel a bit too hack & slash (or point & shoot). It becomes less of a tense encounter, which if to do the original justice - is how it should feel, and more of hacking/gunning through a mob of enemies to get to your objective.  

I'm intrigued by the RPG elements, winning over faction members to develop specific skills, watching relationships change based on decisions made during missions and having skill checks in the open world. From what I've seen so far this looks promising (although watching your character attempt a skill, and using a probability mechanic to determine success rather than having it blocked off altogether if your stat isn't high enough would work better for me).  

There isn't the sense of battling "against the Zone" - so improved survival mechanics will be welcome. At the moment I'm collecting resources to expand my base - in the original I was able to decide who ate, who ate less, and who went to bed hungry whilst being worried about who would up sticks and simply walk out on me.  

For the atmosphere - again I'm mixed. The original had the sense of weirdness "breaking in", here it's taken everything over with some weird Chernoyblite winged beastie encountered in the first area of the game. This is tough-- it changes the tone but in the same vein I don't think it would have worked to have remade the first game (a'la Stalker). It's less a continuation of the story, more of a development of the concept... what would happen if Chernobyilite was harnessed on a commercial scale? It's taking some time to grow on me.

On the picky side, I'm not won over by the modelling of the main character... when downing bad guys / mutants lets have an option to autoloot... having to hold down a button to crouch is slightly annoying  (because the delay is just long enough to irritate me)- and am I the only one who found the English voices a little jarring?

Despite all this, I've kind of enjoyed it so far.  Reading the updates from the devs I'm excited. There's a lot of passion going into this and I'm confident they'll iron out the quirks and rework this into something on par with the first game. I'll stick with it and looking forward to the August update. 

i7-10700F
GTX 4060
32 GB RAM

Megapatch 3: 1 hour in after restart. Removal of the class system I think was a wise move. Enjoying the open world atmosphere although there seems to be a bit too much open space at the moment (although I've found a bunker which I need a charge to open, so that looks interesting). Some of the monster animations seem clunky when there's several on screen - which is annoying as things were fine pre-patch.

Megapatch 4: Sorry to write this. I realise its EA but I don't always have the patience. Crashed straight to desktop as soon as I used a teleporter. Frame-generation looks to tank the game (at least on my rig). Load times are slow, textures take while to load in. Inventory menu access is sluggish. Could be because I'm running off a HDD - but with 32GB and a 4060 GTX where performance was fine on MP3 and earlier builds this is a disappointment. Think I'll shelve this one for now. There's no fun starting/tweaking/restarting a game in the hope it'll be playable on the next launch.

review:
The game clearly has a lot things going on and you can understand that a great potential is there but it suffers in aspects that are somewhat common both in AAA titles and indie as well.

1. No clear vision of what the game wants to be. Developers say that this is not Stalker and it aims to be a survival horror with base building and that is respectable. Well frankly i cant feel any horror or special atmosphere since the game feels more like a Simcity in exclusion zone with the bonus that you can see your world from first or third pov camera. Too much expanded base building, i mean come on i even set up electrical lanes for the base what more can i say? Add a water pipe system and you got Simcity there. Feels like it is there to make the game feel more content rich, something like Assassins Creed with the countless brain dead side quests to i dont know collect 123123 feathers from the building roofs for the achievement or to be 100% in your game completion bar.

2. Optimization is really bad like in the majority of UE5 games, Stalker 2 included while the graphical outcome is something that doesnt justify this at all. It is really disappointing to see things like these and from the other hand you play free mods like Improved Weapons Pack OR Anomaly Custom and see projects like IX Ray and Open Xray which have improved a 20y old graphical engine offering respectable graphics with good performance and most important of all IMMERSION.

3. Gunplay and melee combat feel really strange. Melee weapons feel like World of Warcraft which means that you hit with a bludgeon weapon and the whole feeling of you hitting and the enemy receive the hit is like i dont know Minecraft. Gunplay is even worse. Taking the example of Improved Weapon Pack modpack for Stalker i shoot with the shotgun and MAN it feels that i actually shoot with a shotgun. Shooting with a shotgun or AK here feels like shooting Nerf from Temu.

The ingredients are here for a really good game in the Exclusion Zone but right now even after the 5th August big patch i would advice people to wait for the final product OR 1 year later in the EA.

Not recommended.

review:
自从用上RPG，BOSS的设计便失去了应有的挑战性与平衡性。当前游戏在优化方面存在明显不足，例如显卡负载过高、模型定位异常、骨骼动画疑似非原创、过场动画交互失效等问题频发。此外，某些软体怪物的建模质量粗糙，视觉效果甚至不及上世纪90年代的作品。在技术飞速发展的2025年，建议相关开发团队重视美术资源与引擎技术的升级，以提升整体游戏品质。

Since the adoption of RPGS, the design of bosses has lost its due challenge and balance. The current game has obvious deficiencies in optimization, such as frequent problems like excessive graphics card load, abnormal model positioning, suspected non-original skeletal animations, and ineffective cutscene interaction. Furthermore, the modeling quality of some soft monsters is rough, and the visual effects are even inferior to those of works from the 1990s. In the year 2025, when technology is advancing at a rapid pace, it is recommended that relevant development teams attach importance to the upgrading of art resources and engine technology to enhance the overall quality of the game.

review:
I love Chernobylite, I 100% the first game, beat it several times, studied the entire story, fell in love with the characters, custom made a physical version of the OST, and created many things inspired off it. I loved it so much that multiple of my friends fell in love with it too from watching me play or hearing me talk about it for months. 

When I heard there was a second game coming out and that it would be co-op, me and my friend immediately wishlisted it. I got the game on release day and played the prologue, but ultimately waited for him to also get the game. He did recently, and so we started playing it.

Booting it up was no problem, although i did experience several GPU failures while trying to get past the first fighting area on the ship. The animations are oddly smooth and uncanny, the mouth visemes look like the characters are overexaggerating their speech, the alpha mapping looks like static. These aren't massive problems, but some things really broke the immersion and feel of the game, like: The map being unrealistic to the Zone, and not just something being moved a little ways away, but some buildings entirely in the wrong places even though the first game prided itself on being so accurate, it feels like a far cry from what it was. The NPCs talk like robots, pronouncing character names wrong, the most notable that I've encountered is Tarakan being pronounced "tear-a-can"?? The voices feel off too, that is NOT what Black Stalker sounded like in the first game. The combat isn't horrible, but it feels sometimes like the game is way too easy and then way too hard. The first boss atop of Prip'yat hospital was really buggy and could 2 shot me, but a gang of raiders I could head shot without them even getting to aggro onto me? The melee combat feels wonky too, sometimes enemies deal inconsistent damage, or I get stun locked by 5 projectiles and 2 Chernohosts ganging on me. The Zone doesn't feel as correct as the first game. I enjoy the open world aspect, but it could definitely be made better with missions or side missions or random events occuring as you run from point A to point B. The story is completely lost on me, I don't really understand anything going on, I have no attachment to any of the characters, they feel shoe-horned, not introduced.

To become friends with Sashko, Mikhail, Tarakan, Olga, and even partially Olivier, you had to earn it. You did missions that would help them, you would talk to them directly and learn about them, they would teach you, help you, do more than just sit at base. The base felt like a home, we all had to put in our own work and together get the materials to survive. Now, I talk to Sonya, she doesn't face me while talking to me, then I get given a task 1000 meters away, so I run there, do it, run back, and mission complete. I also don't understand why I can't just go do something, why do I have to talk to Black Stalker for something? Why is Black Stalker called that in the tablet if we only know him as Igor? Why do people say "ku-mu-nuck" instead of how it should be pronounced naturally? 

I have many opinions and views on this game, it works better on its own, not as a sequel. It feels like Fallout 4 instead of Metro or STALKER, like the original game. It feels like the devs tried to do too much extra and lost its roots in the process. I pray to god the devs read this and this becomes a No Man's Sky scenario: horrible launch, amazing a few years later. If I could help the development process, I would. I just hope it returns to a survival game with proper story and emotional attachment instead of a glorified Fallout.

I don't recommend it right now, although down the line it may be better to play.

review:
[h1]The "over the top" positive reviews, not correct [/h1]

Current reviews are not truly honest because they do not address fundamental issues with this game. Has to be internal or people just being nice to get some review understanding. 

We are here to save your money and interest, not provide information that would be otherwise unhelpful to the team developing the game.
We would rather be honest, provide feedback, assist with corrections, and expose our passion or lack thereof for their work, rather than boost sales for a fundamentally flawed game.
Fun at first, but replayability will not be there once you do it all, unless they add lots more.
The gruel, without flow, running yourself ragged because you can't hire help for the departments you have, is the killer. 

Who wants to run day after day with a lottery labor pool of applicants?

Too many problems in design, as previously stated, driving our team bananas. 

Was enjoyable for the first five minutes, then when things got going.. good lord... just want to stop playing.

The only analogy... proverbial... "How many times do you need to be punched in the face before relocating your entire presence, before you have enough?" 
Well, I just went 10 rounds with Mike Tyson, in our analogy, and four of six of us feel nothing but regret. Games are made to be fun, challenging, satisfying, emotionally connected to a character or environment, and never regret.

The amount of bugs that are present, lack of content, design, fundamental issues, in the short play durability/replay ability, ect.
Don't get us wrong, its a fun little game for $7 or under, a dollar more is pushing it so get it on sale if you must but you will refund after an hour unless they are all hands on deck making HUGE development, time-consuming, well planned changes.

[h1]In closing:[/h1]
Fair price for $7, while on sale at best. Not a penny more.

[h1]Our opinion to grow the game:[/h1]
