review:
I really wanted to like this game, but I couldn't really get into it after trying to fly around for a few hours and testing a few of the mechanics. I usually LOVE plane games, but this one left a bad taste in my mouth in a few ways.

The main mechanic of the game, the flying, feels poorly designed.
- If you use any rudder or elevator AT ALL, your speed tanks. Not sure if this is supposed to be more percentage based, but at the moment of writing this, you loose just as much speed at 1% rudder as you do at full.
- Speed feels off in more ways than one. I know you're literally flying a boat, but when the speedometer shows 350 KNOTS (which is faster than some fighter planes in WWII) and you still feel like you're moving slow, then I'm not sure what is going on.
- On the note of speed, the faster you go the more rotation you gain while using your control surfaces. Probably realistic, but playing on a controller was hard on its own. Not sure what playing on keyboard would be like as I didn't dare try. Maybe cutting down on the input curve for the rotation speed would help the player?
- The boost is cool, but you literally lose control of your aircraft while doing so. If you make the mistake of pulling up while boosting, you might just enter a perpetual loop that you cannot escape. I crashed a couple of times like this with different pilots.
- Overall, I felt like the flying became a second thought over all the other strange and offputting mechanics in the game. I'm glad I never got into a dogfight. I doubt I would be able to do anything of note.

I have a few gripes about the UI as well.
- It feels largely unintuitive and is clunky to get around. I started using the controller to get around, but quickly realized it was nearly impossible to figure out which button the game was focusing on.
- Even with mouse and keyboard I had to press some buttons multiple times in order for them to do something. Was this due to the controller having a button selected somehow?
- Inventory management was fine, but left something to be desired. You have so little space in your plane, you can fit a few apples and a few grapes in there, which you can bring back to make brews with, but overall I felt like going back and forth 3 times to make one batch is too much with how the flying feels.

* I cannot say this for sure, but the VOs almost sound like AI? It sounds a bit unnatural sometimes. Not hating on the VOs at all if that's not the case. It's mostly the end of some of the sentences where the tone sounds weird. *


Overall, all I can say is this. In the current state of the game, if you're looking for a nice flight based exploration game, this is not it. If they fixed the controls and feel of the plane, then perhaps.

review:
Edit with more playtime: Unfortunately the game has been getting worse, not better, with patches. I routinely get bugs that result in progress wipes, freeze controls, and now I cannot finish the final mission because the game soft-locks during the final boss fight. I regret ever buying it.

TLDR: Although the game has a solid base, it needs some more time to cook. Check it again in a few months maybe.

Ok, so the base game is pretty simple: you fly around and collect ingredients to turn into alcoholic beverages that you sell to scattered bars. The base gameplay is good, with a satisfying (although sometimes wonky) flight model, reasonable difficulty (most of the time), a beautiful setting and interesting characters. Flying around in this game is just fun, and checking out the different islands is nice. The characters all have different missions that add some variety to the basic gameplay loop, and different traits that make different builds for different missions worthwhile to explore.

But... the game really needs some time to go through balancing, bug fixing and content adding. I'm finding plenty of bugs and although the developers are quick about putting out patches this is stuff that should have been fixed a while ago. Gathering ingredients can be hit or miss, with those you shoot taking no time at all while those on farms you have to bomb or scythe are pure, tedious frustration. The enemies are, for the most part, just window dressing, they never really come after you, just hang around flying in circles and taking shots at you with their turrets. Some of the boss battles are interesting even if the objective is unclear, but others are awful; I can into a submarine that wouldn't let me leave the island until I defeated it, turning a quick flight out to pick up some ingredients into a tedious boss battle in a plane built for ingredient gathering. The game is a long series of this, with plenty of fun mixed in with frustration from poor design choices and bugs that will take a while to settle.

Finally, the game has a weird inconsistent "gentle" vibe to it. On one hand, it's literally called Brew Barons and you deliver hard liquor to bars, but there is a screen before the game that oh no the developers don't condone drinking. But one pair of characters' mission is to fly drunk around and cause property damage...? You shoot water bolts at the enemies and they're never defeated, just run away, while the pirates are clearly some sort of smog-spewing Captain Planet C-villains, but there is a clear drumbeat of military stuff going on in the game and the whole ingredient gathering is very violent. It feels like they switched directions mid-stream and it makes for a lot of jarring moments.

review:
Too much going on and too little time.
The demo didn't make this seem too ambitious. But in execution, this wasn't a very fun experience overall.

Starting with the pros, it has a great art style, great world and concept for that matter. Exploring the map was fun, it left me jaw dropped because of how gorgeous and well crafted it is. The scale too was impressive. The fact the islands were only part of the map is another big surprise. And it’s well optimized. 

But the cons are many, I got 10 hours through on Medium Difficulty, done over 30 contracts, discovered over 6 new islands. And this is where it falls apart essentially.

Story, doesn’t really have much of one? It’s really just exploration, brews, and pirates. Each character has their own backstory which is nice I suppose. 

By far the most cons come from the gameplay. From the start, the tutorial is very brief and as a result leaves you in the dark. I’m on the autism spectrum and have learning difficulties and this game was way too overwhelming in some areas. Tutorials after the start though were non-existent. I found myself having to go to the controls to figure out how to do things, even things tied to the gameplay that you’re not told about.

The plane controls were odd? It felt different to other games, I used mouse controlled here though I am used to keyboard, find mouse a bit more precise. It’s the way the plane moves, it feels slow and feels like it’s not very well polished… regardless of the upgrades that come later.

The brewing aspect would have been fun if, you didn’t have to pick up every recipe through exploration/experimentation, and be able to reset a brew you finished in case of a mistake, as before a patch this didn’t have a quality of life to show the contracts.

Contracts I feel mixed on. They’re straightforward with what they want and you have to deliver a higher quality to sell, the higher the quality the more the money. Problem is, this ties to recipes again, and has many secrets it seems to achieve the best quality. So the start of the game feels extremely slow, I was only able to get speed upgrades for my plane in my 8th hour roughly.

The bar is strange too, the fact you can’t serve every drink you make at a profit, not to mention it not making much profit at that. It feels overly complicated in that aspect too. Probably scratches an itch for those who like managing stuff. Not for me though.

The hangar is by far one of the most bizarre choices. This game at this point I realize prioritises realism over fiction… because there’s friction everywhere. And I mean, everywhere. Dink your plane a bit? You can’t move much anymore, and have to pay a portion of your gold. Want to harvest more wheat? Replace your wing entirely for gold and if you want to go back, pay gold. Catalogue is also very overwhelming to look at with so much text. Also the stats for the plane too. 

The Roster system is a bit complicated too. And finnicky in terms of UI. Forgot to mention, the UI is very finnicky. Sometimes pressing tabs in menus doesn’t do anything. 

Exploration whilst it has its pros, it all seems to be a bit of a memory game. But the ingredient gathering is arguably one of the worst aspects of it. The winching minigame is annoying in itself (not to mention rare even when exploring multiple islands). I never really enjoyed gathering ingredients, which can also be very bugged too. Like the suction radius when gathering them is extremely small. Some ingredients are just hard to spot like Whispywheat, which I had no clue on how to get until I asked in the community. But this type of ingredient is a pain too because of how slow it is to gather. Getting to it is a problem in itself. Then there’s underwater ingredients which despite how easy it is to spot ingredients on land and air, it was impossible to see underwater until you’re close by and at day time. There’s no indicator on where these ingredients are so you have no idea where to drop water bombs on then. Also the waterbomb crosshair is very bugged. It isn’t landing where the crosshair is, the crosshair keeps glitching out, and it doesn’t always dislodge ingredients… 

Combat, well, what little I did of it, was just a pain. First I found a plane that was marked for me to take down… shot it for over 5 minutes with water bolts and it wasn’t going down. So I don’t know what that was about. Second, found pirates harvesting from an island. They sent out planes to fight me which luckily were fairly easy to take down, but this giant plane was not. As there was no obvious way to dodge attacks (Other than the top one where the gun fires everywhere, where you just go beneath it). And it seemed to have a massive health pool as well, but got shot down before I was able to see how much I could damage it. My third encounter was on an island opposite where they had an airship. I turned away because I knew this was pointless. But things got worse. All the friendly islands got invaded by pirates with, submarines. This was even more of a pain than the first two. Because there were no obvious weakspots, had no clue what to aim at. I was getting missiles thrown at me, with the only way to take them down being to shoot them. Then the submarines disappeared when I was shooting them (Submerged I guess) only to reappear, then I get shot down before I could even get an angle on them, and now the island is held hostage. 

New contract? What’s this abo- what the hell is Caramel Carrot? Seriously, why am I getting contracts for ingredients I not only can’t get to, but have no recipes for? I get there’s a deadline for accepting contracts and delivering them, but I don’t get why there’s contracts for things I don’t have or have not discovered yet. 

But by far the most baffling thing to me is the withholding of information which ties to everything. This ties to pretty much everything on the list. There’s nobody to say “Hey, you got a contract for X ingredient? You can find that in X by flying into the streams.” Or “This plane is heavily armoured, you might need to come back another time.” This paired with the gameplay loop of going out to get ingredients, deliver everything even, just makes things so arbitrary and tedious. I would have been happy if this was even a 8 hour game with a linear story and a lot of quality of life options.

Small but annoying things:
I sometimes lost brews when transporting them (All safe landings where unsafe can leave damage or lose brews/ingredients)
Gathering of water is tedious.
Island boosting upgrade which is useful, unfortunately has the caveat of you looking to look at a logo in the sky… and it also doesn’t trigger all the time. Not sure if it’s because of distance or what?
Which reminds me, water bolt and water bomb’s distance is quite underwhelming. It would have been great to have an upgrade at least to make these hit from further away. 

If it isn’t obvious by this point, I don’t recommend. I was really looking forward to playing this game. And the first few hours were great, but I Immediately noticed these issues when they first appeared. Plus if I need to use the internet to play the game for me… is it really playing at all? I’m really frustrated, probably having a meltdown without realizing it. If a lot of these issues are patched I might consider coming back, but I don’t really have any hope at this point. I was having a bad day as of writing this too.

review:
Pulled this up after catching a glimpse of it in an unrelated review of PC hardware, and I'm a little mixed on whether or not to recommend this.

I haven't played as far into the game as I'd like to at the moment to give the most comprehensive review, though after an evening thumbing through the early game, I can at least offer a few thoughts on what may or may not matter to you at a glance.

Gameplay wise you'll find there's a bit more emphasis on the gathering aspects of the game when it comes to making most of your income and pleasing other folks in the setting.  I think it's a terribly fun way to tie yourself to the world and the resources it has to offer, and the brewing minigame is plenty fun to keep you occupied while you're grounded!  Ingredients are collected through various methods involving your plane, from shooting fruits from trees, to running your plane through fields of wheat; all methods have a nice balance of risk to reward, more or less.  Plenty of players have pointed out the tedium of water bombing ingredients, and it's something I've noticed as well.  Apparently the devs are quite active on improving the game over time, so I expect some balancing to be done at some point in the future.

UI/UX is a little clunky as well, as others have noted.  It works well enough, but I've found myself getting the cursor "caught" on certain buttons and elements of the UI, and sometimes it's difficult to tell where your cursor will end up if you're using a controller.  Mouse and Keyboard cursor inputs through the UI can also be a hassle, and I've found it generally easier to just default to a controller.  Again, this is something many are suggesting will be addressed by the dev team as they're bolstered by the initial sales and feedback.  Outside of these quibbles, though, I feel like the piloting controls respond as I'd expect they would from an arcade flying game, so it gets a pass where it matters the most!

Updated as of 2026: The devs have added an AI disclaimer of using AI to generate speech in the game, when, in reality, there was far more that AI had been used to generate in this game like portraits and dialogue.

At this point, I'm completely against having AI in any component of a game's development, no matter the size of the team or scope of the game.

Brew Barons is one of those games that should be great, it has most of the right ingredients. That said, after playing it for nearly six hours and still being relatively early on in the game, I just don't have any desire to come back to it.

I do find the fact that you shoot water instead of bullets to be a bit out of place, especially since this is a game where you are brewing alcohol and dealing with characters with some really grown up flaws. It's like the game couldn't decide whether it is aimed at kids or adults.

The whole harvesting by shooting at stuff is also a bit silly. This becomes old quickly and I feel like it could have been implemented differently.

As it stands, it's a okay game with a really interesting graphics style and decent flight mechanics, that doesn't quite live up to its potential. You might have some fun with this one, but as far as combat flight games go there are better options out there.

review:
I'd love to recommend this game because it can be so much fun, but there is a litany of issues. They haven't updated it with any meaningful content maybe ever (they added some plane parts but they kind of suck for the most part). The plane parts should be focused towards a specific thing so you can build your plane to either harvest wheat, or tree resources, or bomb resources. It also falls short in combat where you need either a fast plane or a strong plane and they both suck against specific enemies even if you build toward combat. The game play loop is enjoyable to me and i could play this for hours if they added more end game content. The pirates are pretty unmanageable if you leave them on since you only have so much time in a day to collect resources and make brews. I hope this isn't an abandoned game, but it feels like they're doing the BARE MINIMUM to make it feel like it isn't. A lot of people bring up the ai voices and yeah they are bad, but really this game isn't a story driven dialogue game.

Overall this has potential to be a great game, but it feels like the updates they do are few and far between (not to mention they include almost no new content apart from plane parts). Really fun, but should probably be about 10$ since it's about 10 hours of content and VERY stale after that.

The brewing minigame is fun, although that does lead me into my first issue, which is that the water ingredients can be hard to spot.

So I had the pleasure to 100% this game and I have had very mixed experience with this title so lets see if I can stay objective.

From the initial description and trailers I assumed this title would be something like war thunder meets some farm sim/ tavern keeper game. 
That is partially correct but the title is unfortunately not perfect and tends to waste a lot of players time due to lack of proper ability to move through the map fast or be able to move around the map better, as even the trading zeppelins where you can dock and purchase ingredients do not help out as much.

I would honestly rate this title 4/10

Pros 
Nice soundtrack
Pleasant graphics 
Easy controls to learn 

Cons
Lot's of wasted time traveling from point A to B! (This is a huge problem in the game) 
Limits in plane builds (you can build light medium heavy plane but the chassey stays relatively same in each of these 3 models you just change things around) 
Bugs (especially if you are taking out the enemy zeppelins and you have to fly inside to destroy the engine a lot of time I did not touch any surface however my plane somehow crashed into the enemy vessel) 
During one mission which takes place inside a cave, I was escaping due to rising tide, did not make it, I warped through the wall suddenly was by the city and I got mission complete status...


Overall the concept is great because if you are a fan of aviation and farming sims it's an interesting blend of ideas, 
but the execution, heavily repetitive exchange between characters bugs and just a lot of wasted time waiting to reach an island to get some ingredients and then travel back it's just not that great unfortunately.

I would only recommend you checking this out during sale.

review:
In it's current state, I just can't recommend it... Yet.
I'll keep this short. Extremely unpolished and bare bones. You find you are trying to convince yourself it's good or to be more patient, which in itself is a bad sign. 
Doesn't hold a candle to competitors doing basically the same thing (7DTD for instance).
It's got some neat ideas but all feels rushed in relation to an evidently premature release day.
I feel I have a thousand notes for the devs of both critical and quality of life changes that need to be made. Not "want", but "need", which is also a bad sign out of the gate. To name just a few?
No character level ups, no character customisation, No body equipment, no headshot bonus damage in a ZOMBIE game, no limb damage, a forced home base, no zombie spawn control, no tool repairs, TINY storage and stack quantities... I could go on for hours.
I'm hoping to come back and change this review in time but it must be said, I'm skeptical in my expectations of this title. In short, It doesn't seem the devs entirely understand what they were setting out for in this title that completely lacks identity. Is it a farming sim or a zombie survivor? Noone knows.

review:
[h2][b][u]Note:[/u][/b][/h2]
 This is a review originally written for [url= https://www.opiumpulses.com] Opium Pulses [/url]. The full article can be found [url= https://www.opiumpulses.com/article/869/the-last-farmer-review] HERE [/url]. Feel free to take a look at the Opium Pulse Steam Curation page [url= https://store.steampowered.com/curator/3800356/] HERE [/url] as well.

The Last Farmer is a survival/horror game by developer Geekon. What will be the developers 15th game release within a year-and a half, one might be slightly pensive as to what sort of quality they’re bringing to the table. If my time spent in-game as well as taking the overwhelmingly trend-specific ratings of prior titles into account: the concerns are entirely well founded. That being said, while there is ABSOLUTELY a market of games that are simply “so bad they’re good”, it seems as though Geekon misses the mark even in that regard. 

Coming-to in a dead-end nook of a desert, your character makes his way to a small overlook, where you find the remnants of a barn, and a conveniently placed natural source of clean water. Within the dilapidated barn, you find a worse-for-wear car (which will turn into a long term project to help aid in your supply runs) and a “conveniently” placed bed, as well as several workstations you’ll need to get up and running to get yourself fully functional for the road ahead, as desolate and clunky as it may be. 
Effectively you’re a farmer in a post-zombie-apocalypse situation, just trying to survive in your “journey of restoration”!

And what a journey it is! Opening strong with poor font spacing during story-board cut scenes and atrocious spelling mistakes within the bare bones tutorial, you’ll be journeying across your keyboard trying to figure out what keys do what. Minimal explanations and no viewable key binding menu, or ability adds to frustrations. While some of the controls feel about par for the industry, the inability to remap or even view them starts players off on a fairly sour note. 

To further add to the magnificently clunky journey, poor optimization, overly sensitive default movement (the default is set to 25, I ended up setting mine to 10 for it to feel “normal”) as well as generally broken setting plague The Last Farmer. Default sound settings end up near muted is the slider is moved more than a few ticks. Music changes suddenly, without warning nor transition, and without any real reason. The audio is bland and uninspired, and grows old quickly.  In addition, the voice acting is relatively bland and awkward, leaving MUCH to be desired. 

As far as visuals go, there is very little to write home about. From your giant Meat Mittens with oddly protruding fingernails to the blatant use of assets slapped left and right, there is not much to see. Picking the barren obscure desert of Texas leave little to be seen, sans randomly placed (and nonsensically designed) homes, abandoned military bases, and odd “points of interest” that have little to be interested in, and seem relatively out of place. In an odd way, it almost feels like the desert was a choice made as an excuse for it to be relatively bare in terms of “filler”. What could have been a relatively promising concept, once again, falls flat.

In a market nearly over saturated in both survival craft as well as zombie titles, you will find plenty of titles that do what is attempted here, but better for near the same cost. While perhaps not hinging on the Farmer aspect as much, games like 7 Days to Die still provide a vastly more entertaining time, and much less frustration. In short, repetitive assets, boring and blurry zombies with the same vocals, uninspired design and just a general lack of effort really make The Last Farmer just about The Last Thing on my list when it comes to Zombie Survival Craft titles.

review:
Alright. [i]The Last FARMER[/i] is a game that released a few weeks ago and is this devs version of a survival game set in a zombie post apocalypse. And it is better than a lot of its Unity store contemporaries. It does however also have quite a few issues that had me double checking just to verify that it wasn't in early access. Because while it is a mostly feature complete game, there are some frustrations that probably could have been ironed out more easily if it WAS in early access. Also, if you scroll down to the purchase part of the product page, it says it is called [i]FARMER SIMULATOR[/i]. And I think that oversight is emblematic of some of the other fairly obvious issues that hopefully also will be fairly uncomplicated to resolve.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3362953036

The story set-up is pretty straightforward. You are a dude who has been scraping by in the post apocalypse, but now you're looking for a place to settle in and simplify life by becoming a farmer. Of course, in order to do so, you will have to fortify the place you find (an old auto shop) and expand it so you can grow crops and hopefully raise livestock. Nothing in life is simple though and the remnants of the area's military have adopted a protection racket, wherein you pay them every few days in produce in order to be protected from them, lol. And from what I can tell, the main story will have you overthrow said group. There not a lot of story and the actual voice acted dialogue where it exists has a fair few comically mispronounced words. Additionally, there are weird gaps after every apostrophe in the notes you find. Such as "it'   s".

You will spend most of your time crafting and exploring with combat interludes. The crafting is all pretty intuitive and will feel familiar to anybody who has played a game featuring such. Nothing crazy there, and it works fine, although the fact that using up an item crafting something doesn't register as having an open inventory slot is a minor issue. All crafted tools have item degradation. Not my favorite gameplay mechanic, but it's not too invasive here. You also have the opportunity to fix up a car and then repair said car after you inevitably run over enough zombies and soldiers to damage it. The car is fun enough to drive, although the game will at times stutter while driving.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3363555060

You will be relying heavily on crafted spears and clubs for combat. Which also have quality degradation as you use them. Clubs are more powerful, but I'd argue they are pretty useless because they have short arm reach and you will be trading with zombies more often than not. They can be effective against soldiers, but there's really zero reason to use clubs when spears are an option. And spears do have the same short arm issue, but the weapon is long enough to where a simple kite and then attack while moving backwards technique works against all zombie types. You can also find firearms. I have only ever found assault rifles. They don't have quality degradation, but ammo is fairly limited and the bullets don't do much damage, so you will waste a fair few on each enemy. A nice thing is the audio when you hit an enemy is different than when you miss, giving you a better indication of when you actually hit something. 

Two issues with firearms beyond the low damage. First off, bullet stacking doesn't work properly in your inventory. Any bullets you add to your already existing stack will not register as being in your inventory for the purposes of reloading your weapon. The only way to circumvent this issue is to split the stack repeatedly until it does register the bullets. The second issue is that for some reason, they have zero monetary value at traders. Which is pretty sucky.

In fact, outside of limited cap value for craftable items, which you aren't going to want to sell, you can only sell food/water/gasoline. All of which you definitely should be trying to hold onto. In fact, from what I can tell, the only item actually worth taking to traders is cooked pumpkin, which gives you 100 caps per. The entire trader system needs to be overhauled IMO. The items they have that you might need are waaaaayyyy overpriced, but you get comparatively nothing when you sell similar items.

Exploration feels pretty good, be it on foot or in your vehicle. However, there are really only a few variations of buildings and there is a lot of space between them. And most building only really spawn seeds, soda, and canned food. And actually, outside of food, craftables, seeds, and occasionally bottle caps, there really isn't any loot to speak of. Very very rarely, you will find a gasoline can.

Some of the building are also unfinished and you will fall through ceilings or floors periodically. And sometimes, you can't get back out because the stairs that are inevitably there are only there visually. You will just walk right through them rather than climb them. Where I stopped playing was when that happened in an actual quest area (The prison cellblock C). There was literally no way to get up the stairs from second to third floor.

Also, default mouse sensitivity is insane. I dropped it down most all the way from whatever it was originally. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3363555045

The thing is, I actually like this game a fair amount. I'd found a few quests that I was wanting to finish. Delivering the occult book to a certain weirdo, finding the photo in the prison, letting an outpost know the military camp had been crushed. But at some point, when the issues stack up, you just gotta call uncle and set it down. I will continue to follow the game and see what the devs do to remedy these issues and any other issues other players have or might report on. It's otherwise a small step above what is a heavily saturated zombie survival game market filled with Unity store assets. I guess they're maybe a bit more proficient using those assets.

 For now, my recommendation would be to hold off on buying it but to give the game a follow and watch how bug fixes and polish updates come through. I will be giving this a thumbs down here due to the lack of a neutral option and the abundance of issues, but via curation, it will receive an informational rating instead.

review:
So I've fairly run out of things to do in only 13 hours.. got a few achievements left to clear but here's my thoughts on this...

If I was able to refund this, I would.   Sorry, but the only collectable resources in the product are as follows:

Resources: Wood planks, sticks, rocks, cloth, fertilizer and seeds (also potato plants).
Food: Cans 3 types, water, soda energy bars (2 types) and potatoes.
Guns: 5 types but you can't seem to craft your own bullets, you need to get them off soldier bodies and even then its 1-17 (mostly on the lower end)
Two types of animals: pigs and chickens and they don't seem to die of starvation at all if you don't feed them.
The buildings...... man all I can say is its literally the most BASIC of building models...    foundation, wall, door, door frame, window, fence, gate, stair and defense walls (which break as easily as falling over a banana peel)... zombies just smash those with no real deterant. 
Only the spikes are any value for defense and those last a little longer.

there's 14 collectable blueprints - that's it.   2-3 machines (fertilizer, biofuel and one other), 3 crop planting blocks 1x3.2x3 and 3x3.  Then its a few weapons (iron axe, iron shovel, iron pickaxe, iron mace, iron spear, machete), a few other minor things like bear trap, metal crate... but overall the recipes are a huge disappointment. Then lastly like 3 upgrades to your car, which drives pretty badly anyhow regarding control.

Three odd quests only which only unlock access to the traders.

You can make one portable workbench which literally only crafts the basics.  The other two workbenches you repair in the garage lets you do the construction buildables (walls, foundations, etc) and the other for the collectable blueprints you find.  But you can't build those workbenches anywhere else... you can only use those in that garage which is at the corner of the map.. so long-a$$ run back and forth if you want to build anything anywhere else.

My overall experience is that this game is literally an asset base package.   Its far, far, far from being a survival game as there's literally barely anything in product except the bare bones of an idea.   At present with its status I would give this a wide berth until there's actually content, because I would not even flag it as replayable.  
Its not abandoned (at least from the posts I've seen), but I certainly cannot justify the $18 price tag when I've bought games for half that with tons more content and certainly are replayable.
I had hopes for this when I saw it and at the time I purchased it, reviews were still positive.  Unsurprising how its already flipped to mixed in a short time of when I bought this.

review:
"The Operator" is a good game, except it isn't actually a game... It is more of an interactive film, where your choice doesn't actually matter, for example, despite several attempts to play for the agency, I couldn't do so, you always have to side with some renegade hacker("HAL"). The game just locks in dialogue options, so you can only comply to progress further in the game. When she reveals her identity, you can't report her, which proves how choice doesn't matter in this game, even the dialogue options aren't that much of a choice, as the respondents largely react similarly. Also, many actions in it don't have consequences, like you can mess up all the tasks hundreds of times, and the game just tells you you are wrong, not the characters, the game, like, you can (in some cases) just blindly click the screen and eventually you will get it right. Or with how you can mess up the bomb diffusal and subsequently kill a federal agent, with no consequences. 
Generally, the game is well made, and I have not found any bugs, but the crippling lack of player agency, and no consequences for wrong choices just make the game unplayable, and I would, therefore, not recommend it to other people, as a game at least. As I said, this isn't a game it is an interactive activity, that uses the mechanics of a game.

The puzzles are mostly "click on the person's face" or "navigate the floor plan", not really anything where you need to connect knowledge or have an idea. Ending feels rushed and pointless. Not really worth the price tag, but I hope the developer can iterate on this formula and make a longer and better game in the future.
name: The Operator

review: Holy cow talk about completely screwing the pooch with your game. What a great idea completely ruined. How on earth is this just it? Way too short, puzzle potential completely unrealized. The fact that this game just ends and isn't a multi playthrough "figure out the good ending" thing is bananas. What a disappointing waste of my time.
name: The Operator

review:
A pure railroad of a story, the 'big reveal' is pretty obvious about 1/3 of the way into the game, and the ending is a massive letdown with no real payoff.

Don't waste your time. Go play Orwell.  It's a far better game.
name: The Operator

review: In my opinion, having a tragic ending is something a story needs to earn. This story did not earn it. I spent less than $15 on this and I still want my money back.
name: The Operator

review:
There are no extra cases to do. only cases you do are tied to the story.
Feels like a missed oppertunity

Story was good. but it feels like it was cut short.
Felt like you were rushed along since there's no side content to drag out the story bits.
name: The Operator

review:
Interesting premise, interesting game up until the terrible ending and apparently if you want it to be more satisfying you need to go to their discord which... why? I paid for a product, it should wrap up nicely in the game itself... I shouldn't have to go to some other outside thing. I don't even mind its a "bad" ending but so much left unsaid and unsolved. Pick it up on sale only, not worth the 14 for a 3 hour game.

Orwell has a similar vibe with different endings where your choices actually matter. In this one... you can lie or tell the truth, work with or against Hal... literally doesn't matter. I tried my best to sell out/rat out Hal and they trusted me with their identity like... what lmao?
name: The Operator

review:
Looks great, is well polished and the ui/interface is nice. If you're looking for a visual novel-type deal it's great, although a bit short. 

If you're looking for Obra Dinn-esque mysteries and puzzles, it's nothing of the sort. There's the main story, which feels like a tutorial for all the tools you'd like to use more in following cases. That's the reason for not recommending. The ui looks cool, the tools would make for great puzzles/cases, and I would really like to play through more cases in this setting. The content just isn't there.
name: The Operator

review:
Original game but this feels like a big demo.
Mechanisms are presented and used only once. No side-quest, everything is about the main quest and nothing else.
I finished it in 2.3h so just a little bit more than the 2h to be refunded so it felt the developer made the story just long enough to not be able to be refunded. Otherwise I would asked for it.

I would love to love this game but it really needs to be deeper, longer.
I hope DLCs will save it.
name: The Operator

review: Excellent first playthrough, but lack of content.
name: The Operator

review:
The game is a missed opportunity, a project that could have been one of my favorite games.

The game starts off very slow, gets quite exciting in the middle, and ends in the worst possible way.

It feels like being on a roller coaster ride where you're stuck on a track and can't explore or solve mysteries freely. The puzzles are either simple or downright pathetic. Anyone who enjoys mysteries and has read a couple of detective novels could finish the game in under 3 hours. There's a part in the game that's quite exciting and was my favorite, but it ends quickly, leaving a bittersweet feeling.

If this game had followed in the footsteps of similar games like Hacknet, it could have been a masterpiece in the genre. Instead, it turned into an interactive movie, like a typical Sony game.

I'd recommend it if you find it for under 5 euros, as it only offers about 4 hours of gameplay at most.
name: The Operator

review:
I would definitely not recommend this game.  It has a neat concept, you're an operator with the "FDI" who helps agents solve their cases which you quickly learn are all connected but in reality you do very little solving. There were really only 2 puzzles to solve and one of them you can fail immediately with no change to the story.  

This game had promise but ultimately it's really short and disappointing.  Maybe pick up when it's on steam sale for 90% off but you can pass till then
name: The Operator

review: Very short game, so bad time per value. The games marketing is deceiving as it initially presents itself as an investigative style of puzzle game, but the investigation is only used as a vehicle for the game to tell it's story rather than being an involved gameplay mechanic. The gameplay involved had very simple and unengaging puzzles (but the bomb defusal was fun). The story was rudimentary and uninspired as the level of detail in which the clues are presented to the player is astounding with a lack of fundamental complexity present in even the most simple of detective novel, this disastrous combination results in the player being able to piece together the gist of the story within the first ten minutes of the game if they have an IQ above room temperature. Overall, Meh.
name: The Operator

review: For the amount of content it has, it's just not worth it. Good game but very lacking. Can be finished in 2h and could be 1h if you could skip all the useless loading parts
name: The Operator

review:
i was triggered played the demo.
I purchased the game was excited . Played the 3-4 hours game- game ended. So dissapointed.
it would be nice if the game was way bigger, and also playing just watching the blue screen without option on skip the in between in game content is annoying.
It would be better if it was like an office environment so was not boring seeing it.
deserves its money tho but my expectations were very high after playing demo but unfortunately .... not
name: The Operator

review: I've played more satisfying mystery/point and click games. The twist wasn't very satisfying and there wasn't much room for lateral thinking.
name: The Operator

review:
The game kind of struggles with what it actually wants you to do and who it wants you to be.

To get started: I really wanted to love this game, because I like researching and playing detective. However you are given a set of tools and expectations to be resourceful, while actually non of it works outside the main storyline. 

As a package it is nicely crafted and for a while it has you engaged, but at some points it expects you to really take control and go beyond the objective ... but only in the exact path the developer(s) have set out for you. The developer(s) haven't realized that it becomes very frustrating, very fast that the game doesn't allow you to explore or make combinations other than that what they exactly have programmed you to do. So encouraging you to think beyond one case, but at the same time limiting your possibilities very much gets your frustrated easily. Sure there is a subpath that you miss sometimes, but you only miss it because all your other attempts to try something different aren't supported (like you can't call anyone on your own or analyse something that isn't supposed to be analyzed). If you don't have any room to play / experiment, you stop doing it and than at some point the game will make fun of you and point out that you have missed something.

Same goes for the dialogs. The game keeps asking you to select an answer while none of it really matters, it is all linear! Again it learns you to make choices, but the choices don't matter so why are they even there than? Just for a single different line of text to go back to the main story path again?

I'll try to give it a go some more when I am less frustrated. But for now, it has got me fed up.
name: The Operator

review:
I wanted to like this game, typically this is right in my wheelhouse. 

However I was finished in less than 3 hours, and it never required much interaction from me. If the entire game had been the lead into more- this had potential.
name: The Operator

review:
Great game, great plot twists, great story, very fun all the way up to the ending.

I'm going to spoil the ending a bit since that's my only complaint.

[spoiler]While I'm sure bad endings are fun for some people, they're not for me. 

I just don't like that it's an "everybody dies" ending regardless of what I do. If I had the option to save everyone and accomplish the objective, I would greatly prefer that.

[/spoiler]

But I'm marking this as not recommended because I personally felt the game was ruined by the ending, if you disagree with me then ok
name: The Operator

review:
I thought The Operator would be like Papers, Please, with a strong gameplay loop. However, it’s purely a narrative-driven game where all mechanisms are subsumed under the plot arc. 

The lore isn’t developed enough, and the duration is artificially inflated by excessive filler, which feels unnecessary given the game’s 2-hour length.

6/10 for the atmosphere.
name: The Operator

review:
The big twist was too obvious. The traitor/s was/were too obvious. At no point was I surprised about the turn of the story, after the first couple of cases.
Ignore my play time - I left my computer on in the background - this game is a bit too short for the price.
I would appreciate being warned next time if what I'm playing is just a prologue to a future game.
name: The Operator

review: Game had potential but it just isn't fun.  One in 1992 nothing even close to this existed I know I was there.  The game has a very annoying cutscene after the first day just a bunch of noises with a blurred lights on a screen.  I wanted an option to skip over this so badly it didn't contribute to anything just sucked time.  The game has some good concepts but it's on rails with no real option to deviate.  Would have been nice to let the player be a little more free in what they find and how that affected the game choices and outcomes.  As it is it's just a story game on rails.
name: The Operator

review:
I enjoyed the game and, right up until its ending, I was sad that it was about to end.

The ending killed it for me. It wasn't a bad twist, it was how forced of a tragic ending it was. If you don't mind spoilers, see below:

[spoiler] Everybody dies. Well, okay, one person is on the run from the law and another is imprisoned for life, but everybody else dies with extra fluff added to the details of what happened to twist the knife even harder that, after everything you did throughout the game, it was all meaningless because you failed. Might as well have had Patrick Star read me the extended cut of the Ugly Barnacle.[/spoiler]

The intensity of the tragic ending was so dramatic, I went online so I could see what I did to get the bad ending because it gave me such bad whiplash. Nope, no bad ending. Just one ending. It didn't earn or build up to leaving me holding an empty bag of misery. It has extra secrets, but because its ending left me feeling the way it did, I don't feel like I have any reason to TRY and learn more. It doesn't feel like there's a point to learning more outside of satisfying the curiosity I was feeling right up until the game kicked me in the crotch.

If you don't mind stories that abruptly end tragically, literally everything else about the game felt solid. I almost want to give this a recommendation. However, with the ending leaving me feel like nothing was accomplished but a few hours burned down the hole, I feel like I can only recommend this with "Play it at your own risk."
name: The Operator

review:
Too short and I picked up on one of the major twists at the very beginning. I would maybe pay 10$CAD or less for something like this, the story feels like it only just started when it ends and only ties up maybe one or two loose ends. The puzzles feel like they're just introducing mechanics when really that's the one and only time you're going to use them, and they aren't very challenging if that's what you're hoping for.

Overall, this feels like it was supposed to be the first chapter in a longer game/narrative, leaving me completely unsatisfied with the ending and the fact they just try to imply the rest of the story in the credits is honestly like spitting in your face. If you just want to feel like a cool agent for a couple of hours and don't care much about the plot get it when it's on decent sale, otherwise this game isn't worth your money or time.
name: The Operator

review:
A very nice but short puzzle-solving visual novel. The writing was enjoyable and the soundtrack is top-notch. The puzzle-solving may not be entirely intuitive at first glance, but the atmosphere of being pulled out of your element at times definitely comes into play.

And it collapses on itself in the end. The suspension of disbelief the writing begs you to undertake to believe that what happened is in any way reasonable to the story's narrative up unto that point is so massive that I wouldn't shoulder it even if I could.
name: The Operator

review: The Operator is disappointingly short and offers little to no challenge, feeling more like a flashy visual novel than an engaging game. It relies heavily on style over substance, using eye-catching visuals to distract from its shallow gameplay. I honestly thought the game was just starting when it ended, but it was setting up for a sequel (Cash grab a this price). If you're looking for depth or meaningful interaction, this title will likely leave you unsatisfied.
name: The Operator

review:
Its a very good looking package, with very very shallow gameplay and story.
Almost every mechanic is done better in another game. I'd be fine with that, nothing new under the sun and all, if the game wasn't remarkably short. I think in an attempt to not overstay its welcome, it leaves before it can get interesting at all.
I genuinely think a longer playtime, more cases, and just a bit more meat on the gameplay side would have made this game amazing.
I could look past a lot of that if the story was good too. And it was, at least up until the end. It's nothing new of course, but I wasn't expecting it to be perfect. I enjoyed it, and felt rewarded when I saw the twists coming. Genuenly very fun.
Then, the ending happened. To keep it light on spoilers, its terribly written sequel bait that makes the events of the game you just played literally not matter at all. 
If they had stuck the landing, It would've been fine, but otherwise, its not worth it.
Go play Orwell then Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes, and you'll get a much better time
name: The Operator

review: I liked the concept and the presentation but the story wasn’t well-developed and I didn’t find the game challenging enough.
name: The Operator

review: This game offers an interesting premise and unique game-play with an incredibly unsatisfying ending. [spoiler]The twist was incredibly well done but the game quite literally let's you marinate in it for a handful of seconds before rolling credits and denying any actual payoff. The ending hardly even makes sense considering the building is a secure government building and there should have theoretically been a swarm of guards all over the escapee within seconds of the breach. [/spoiler] Maybe I just have trouble suspending my belief but it was fairly upsetting to see a story with so much steam fall flat on its face in the final moments.
name: The Operator

review:
In fact, it is more of an interactive novel than a game. The gameplay is very limited and simple, the choices in the dialogues don't affect anything. And finally, the game is very short. And this is not a matter of price, but of immersion.
Unfortunately, I can't recommend this game.
name: The Operator

review: Too short, no skip function, strange blurry transition scenes and choices that don't have an impact on the story.
name: The Operator

review: Extremely short, mystery ultimately quite easy to see coming, no ability to change your fate.
name: The Operator

review: too short for the $
name: The Operator

review: I really can't 100% recommend, nor 100% not recommend this game. UI and gameplay are fine. The story is well written. It's just too short; only lasted around 2 hours, and was super simple. Ending wasn't great. If it's on sale, play it. Otherwise, don't bother, till something else comes out that makes it more fulfilling.
name: The Operator

review:
If you think this is a game where you analyze crimes while searching for increasingly complicated data you are wrong.
If you think this is a narrative game with multiple branches and endings depending on your decisions you are wrong.

Its just a linear visual novel... and was sold to me as something different.
name: The Operator

review:
The game was fun and interesting-right up until the end-in my personal opinion. I wish there was more to do for the cost, if you're looking into purchasing I would suggest waiting for a sale. 

[spoiler] The ending is very abrupt and leaves me feeling unaccomplished, which is not the reason I personally play games. Sure, I [i] suppose [/i] the story is concluded and the loose ends tied, but in a very disappointing and somewhat lazy way (again, in my opinion). None of your actions really make a difference since the story ends only one way, which is usually fine when the one ending is satisfying in some way, shape, or form. [/spoiler]
name: The Operator

review: No matter what you do, there is only one ending. Don't worry about any of the choices - they don't matter at all.
name: The Operator

I figured the puzzles would get more difficult and the examination and clue connection more complex. However, the game just ended. It was maybe two hours of play - a little more. Not enough to justify the price. Felt more like demo length. The story was good, though it didn't take long to figure out the "mystery" or at least a portion of it. name: The Operator

review: All in all, cleverly made but a bit shorter than I would have liked. Ending felt rushed, leaving more questions than an ending - potentially teasing for a sequel. Left a "it could have been so much more" taste in my mouth.
name: The Operator

review: I need to give this game a thumb down, trust me it is a great game and fun to try and find out everything, but realy 5 hrs to finish a game is way to short thats why i need to give it a thumb down
name: The Operator

review: Very cool first hour, very boring after it throws away the cool stuff it introduced. Play Golden Idol
name: The Operator

review: For the price I paid, it's a bit underwhelming. I predicted almost every twist and I'm usually not good at that. The dialogue choices didn't really seem like choices at all, as I often received 2 options that said the same thing, in different words. Very limited "puzzle" aspect to the game. Interesting concept but just kind of bland. Soundtrack is neat though.
name: The Operator

review:
I've been really into narrative puzzle games lately and was excited to give this one a shot. The gameplay and interface are really tight and the story is interesting. However, in terms of a puzzle game it never feels like it ramps up. The story is broken up into such small pieces that there's no real need to sift through different possibilities. Every step towards solution seems pretty obvious. There are fun mechanics introduced and then only used once. You're never really challenged to combine the skills or info you have gathered over the course of the game. In the end it feels like a kind of short visual narrative with a fun interface. If they made another one focused on more difficult scenarios and a wider scope I would probably try it.

Also, nobody had cell phones or digital cameras in 1992/3. Not sure why they chose to set the game in that particular time period, it makes a lot of the technology feel very out of place.
name: The Operator

review:
I don't think this game is quite what I expected. It's a style of game I'd love to see more of. But while I still mostly enjoyed my time with it, I'm left wanting more.

The story itself is interesting and has enough of those classic thriller movie twist and turns to keep you engaged throughout. Role-playing the "man in the chair" is pretty fun, and you have a few moments that deliver on that promise, at least from a narrative standpoint.

After playing this through once, you'd think the game had multiple endings. You are left wondering if maybe there's some way to correct your mistakes and change the outcome. That is not the case. The ending is pretty bleak, comes pretty quickly (the game itself only being a few hours long at most), and doesn't bring the story to a proper close. I can do without a "good ending", but there's a disappointing lack of closure here.

Broadly speaking, The Operator fails to deliver on the use of "detective skills" it says you'll need in the game's description. You definitely interact with a computer and run a few faux-terminal commands, but most of the time you're just finding a name or a face by clicking the a button that Zoom-Enhances a video CSI style. It sure looks like you're doing the work, but none of it is very challenging and it all feels a little superficial.

There's maybe one section that raises the difficulty and that's because it puts you on a timer and forces you to read an instruction manual. It's the first and only challenging moment the game offers. It was actually a pretty good moment, and the game could have done with a few more scenes this.

I'd not recommend this game to fans of puzzle games who are looking for a challenge, but it's still a fun journey if you want to spend a few hours in the world of a thriller movie. Just don't expect a satisfying ending.
name: The Operator

review: Maybe I'll change this review after playing a little more, but I'm personally not a fan of a game that forces you into situations that make no sense for the character you see. I'm sorry, but [spoiler]no federal agent on their second day is going to hear from a criminal and just agree to a deal. Or at least I am given no reason as to why they would do that other than to progress the plot, and that feels like sloppy writing. Heck if that's the case why even give me the option to tell the truth or lie before. If Evan is so after the truth that he doesn't care, why would he talk about Hal to his supervisor? That would feel better than this. I don't mind visual novels/linear story lines, but I do mind it when a game acts like you have choices and you don't. [/spoiler]
name: The Operator

review: While "The Operator" presents an intriguing premise of managing a mysterious phone service, the gameplay quickly falls flat due to its repetitive mechanics and lack of meaningful progression. The story, though initially promising, fails to deliver a compelling narrative, and the limited interactions quickly become tiresome. The user interface feels clunky, and the overall experience can feel more like a chore than an engaging game. Unless you're a fan of minimalistic simulators with little reward, you might want to skip this one.
name: The Operator

review: Gameplay is interesting but the movies and story is boring.
name: The Operator

review:
To the question of whether I'd recommend this game: it depends, but probably not. 

Full disclosure up-front: I knew nothing about this game, nor had I done any investigating as to what the game was ultimately meant to be, so my reactions here are likely influenced by it not being quite what I expected or really wanted. 

The Operator is a ultimately a fairly short, story-based narrative dressed in the clothing of a detective game, rather than a detective game where you work through puzzles and solve mysteries. 

The game's mechanics and design were an interesting approach to storytelling, but felt quite underused, which probably goes more to my expectations of wanting a detective puzzle game with a greater variety in cases to solve. In most instances a new mechanic was introduced for one section, only for it to never be used again. 

The story itself is passable. I've consumed my fair share of content in the thriller, detective, mystery and conspiracy genres, and nothing here felt fresh to me in terms of the plot; you could see where the story was going from a mile away and the ultimate outcomes fairly early on. 

If you want a mystery story with conspiracy elements woven in, then this is probably worth a go. If that's not what you're in the market for, then you can probably give this a miss.
name: The Operator

review:
What starts out as a fun little puzzle game with an interesting overarching narrative turns in to budget Simulacra, or tin foil hat, the game. It gets really silly the further it goes on and made me actively cringe on a couple of occasions. It's Conspiracy Horror of the most cringe-worthy kind.

If you have cash to burn and need to kill 3 hours then maybe, but to be honest I'd recommend dozens of games before I suggest this. It's a real shame considering the promise it started out with.
name: The Operator

review:
Promising game but fails to deliver. 

The game barely allows you to look for answers or solutions yourself as you must mostly rely on asking other characters for help, including during some of the most high-stakes moments of the story. This makes playing the game a rather passive experience, something you definitely don't want while playing a so-called "detective game"

It occasionaly introduces some interesting mechanisms (i was looking forward to trying the [spoiler]chemscan[/spoiler] again after learning how to use it), but then fails to include them throughout the story. Overall, it doesn't really let you "deduce" much past the first few days.

The ending is pretty abrubt and unsatisfying, as it leaves a lot of plotpoints unresolved and comes off as a bad cliffhanger for a second opus.

Overall, the game seems to be more preoccupied with its storytelling (which was not bad!) than with its gameplay (not great). Could've been a pretty good short film, but I don't recommend it as a game. It doesn't seem to trust their player or itself enough to rely on more complex game mechanics than simply "clicking the button when asked".
name: The Operator

review: I don't quite understand, I was expecting some game play, but there was none. 'DVD simulator' maybe, but you only get to watch 1 ai generated movie and use the play button, occasionally.
name: The Operator

review: Exciting mechanics but if you enjoy the investigation aspects of a game tagged with investigation, the rest is kind of a waste of time. Not enough of a puzzle to stimulate and the payoff is laughable. Just short enough to make you feel like there should be more *and* that you wasted your time.
name: The Operator

review:
I wanted to like this game, and for the four hours I played, it was enjoyable, but not great. 

Pros:
* Creative mechanics are employed here, it has good promise
* There were some good AHA! moments that were fun
* This is a personal one, but I always appreciate when developers make it playable on my Mac Air

Cons:
* This is really more an interactive novel with some puzzle elements than a game. In addition to its short play time, your choices have little to no impact, it really doesn't matter what you choose in many conversations. 
* There's a lot of moments between the actual gameplay bits that feel like time padding, like I would have skipped if given the chance. 
* The writing is just ok, nothing special. The characters could be fleshed out a bit more, I think
* Without spoiling anything, the ending is pretty unsatisfying imo.

Overall, just an ok game, but could be great. I hope the developers continue to grow.
name: The Operator

review:
I really like the genre of mystery games but The Operator felt like it fell short in a few categories for me to recommend this as is. I think they tried to do some interesting things, but I found the story to be a little too 'on rails' for me, and a little too short for the price point. 

One way I'd describe TO is to imagine the intro to a story where you're shown a vast map of the world with a story about it's history and maybe even a quick introduction to the strange artifact you'll be using to navigate the world... And then to only interact with 3% of the map, and to gloss over the history, and the artifact is just a paperweight that we'll never use more than once. That's fine but it does feel like someone went through a lot of trouble to flesh out this world only for it to shrink down to a tiny slice of what they'd made. 

Personally, I'm also not a huge fan of the story. I think they tried to go in a series of different directions at the same time (are you going to play it by the straight and narrow? Are you going to go rogue?) and it all led to the same one place so none of your choices really mattered. The big reveal hinges on you believing that the game's limitations are intentional and not a contrivance of some grand design, so the payout for their big reveals never really felt as good as they could've been. 

So... yeah? I think the story's a little weak/ watered down, but it lives in a frame that I could see the developer building into a bigger/ broader story that would be fun to play. The bones are here for something that could be a cool mystery game, but I'd sooner recommend 'The Roottrees are dead' if you're looking for a better/ more rewarding mystery to sink your time into.
name: The Operator

review:
This game has everything you need for a great game, but then it falls short. Literaly its SHORT. SUPER SHORT. When you think the story get's rolling, the only thing that gets rolling are the credits. I have never been that dissapointed in a game, and I played mass effect 3 with it's amateur ending.
The only thing I can say 

DO NOT BUY!!!

Take you money and go watch a movie or buy yourself a book, even with a bad one at least you get a proper ending.
This game wasted so much potential. It's like the devs had the beginning of a great story, started to program the game before they had the story completed. And after chapter one they ran out of steam but published the game with a makeshift ending. 

AGAIN DO NOT BUY!!
name: The Operator

review:
The game is extremely short and the puzzles are pretty much on guide rails and don't take much effort. The only difficult puzzle was the bomb but only due to the manual not making much sense. The entire game took me just under 4 hours but at least 30 minutes of that was somewhat needless transition footage that I wanted to skip and had almost zero impact on the game.

I had the twist figured out half way through the game and the ending was pretty obvious. I got the game on sale for $10.49 and justify it to myself that a movie ticket probably costs more these days. I was highly disappointed in the very small bit of content and how easy the puzzles were. The production wasn't bad, the concept wasn't bad, and there weren't any bugs I ran into so if there were an option between yes and no for recommendations I would choose that.
name: The Operator

review: i wanted an actual investigate game not just a couple investigations then hey look a bigger conspiracy. they give you multiple programs to only use once and never use again, i had high hopes for this game but i am left ultimately disappointed
name: The Operator

review: The game is way too short and lacks variety.
name: The Operator

review:
This is like the walking simulator of detective games. Don't go into this game expecting deduction gameplay as in Return of the Obra Dinn or The Roottrees Are Dead. While the game has a handful of genuinely fun puzzles and some cool twists and ideas, they're presented extremely linearly, and the latter half of this 3-hour game is basically one extended cutscene. 

Normally this wouldn't be enough for me to give a negative review, but this game explicitly markets itself as a detective game where you "solve crimes". And you really don't. For a price of about half the two aforementioned detective games, you get a fraction of the gameplay, and not that much more narrative.
name: The Operator

review: This was mostly fun, a little short. YMMV, but I think this totally s***s the bed at the end. There's a 'mystery' that I figured out about 10 minutes into the game, and the ending... ugh. [spoiler]I like a dark ending as much as the next guy, but this just felt rushed and unsatisfying,[/spoiler]
name: The Operator

review:
Not 5 minutes into the game the illusion explodes and you realize there are no consequences to your choices.
A hacker who opportunistically deus-ex-machina a missing video part he has and will only release to you, if you say I WILL MAKE A DEAL/  YOU HAVE TO SAY YOU MAKE THE DEAL.
There had been SIX FUCKING LINES, to finally force the player to go THAT way, and I shit you not: "say it, say we have a deal". And frankly, at this point I'm not even that involved in the story, I don't see why the hell I'm forced to comply.
An RPG GM doing that simply loses his Table and his players.
That's lame writing and storytelling..
name: The Operator

review: It's a cool game with a nice gameplay. It even gives you the illusion of a choice. But the ending is very depressing and kinda ruined the whole thing for me. So I can't recommend it.
name: The Operator

review:
A complete disappointment.

1. The gameplay is primitive and boring. Games like Cyber Manhunt or Orwell do this concept much better, in my opinion—they’re more engaging and last longer. The cutscenes drag on, and while you can see why they're there for certain moments... those moments are painfully obvious within the first hour of playing and after that, they seem redundant.
2. The story is shallow and uninteresting. The main twist is something you figure out in the first hour—[spoiler]namely, that your protagonist is Sasha Cole (thanks to the opening scene, the emphasis on Mia COLE, and the fact that your character starts hallucinating when the agent recalls her love for singing). Once you realize that, it’s immediately clear that your friend is the mole, while the "obviously" unfriendly boss is actually a good guy.[/spoiler] This one dumb decision ruins the rest of the game—there’s no wow factor, no payoff.
3. The lore? There isn’t any. Nothing is properly revealed or explained. They just threw in a bunch of medical and chemical terms and called it a day. [spoiler]Who is the Ghost? Why can he effortlessly kill trained agents? What’s the deal with the Organization? The game explains nothing—guess we’ll have to wait for a sequel instead of getting a proper, finished story.[/spoiler]
4. The ending... It left me completely deflated. [spoiler]I hate "everybody dies" endings more than anything, especially when the game tries to pretend it’s being "nonlinear."[/spoiler]
5. It’s very short. Less than three hours to finish.

review:
TLDR - would not buy. knowing this is a movie you just nudge along.
Linear game, where choices don't matter at all. Interesting story-line, and puzzles you'll only solve once, but not enough to justify paying even half price for the game (from an enjoyment/replay value perspective). It's a one and done, no replay value whatsoever. Better off watching a play-through on YouTube.

PROS, but:
All elements of the game could be built towards a randomized investigative type game (look at "Papers, please" or the game described below and then apply the principles to this type of game play).  
Bomb-defusal mini-game was innovative and tense, could have multiple scenarios play out.

A similar type of game that accomplished this was Sid Meier's Covert Operations. If the type of game-play "The Operator" presents is what you're looking for and you can stomach very retro gaming (this was an DOS era game), would recommend checking out Covert Operations instead.

But again, the story is compelling. Will look to see if the sequel's gaming experience expands in a way I was hoping this game would play out: not as a movie, but a game where the player has actual agency in the world.

To the Devs:
You have a lot of components in hand to assemble a compelling, unique "radiant" type investigative game with an engaging story (or stories) lying beneath the surface to draw the player into the game's world. Looking forward with cautious optimism to see how the sequel(s) plays out.

To simplify (somewhat) integrating multiple endings (and this doesn't have to be visible to the players, or could be some sort of end of day report/summary), continue with the the day to day system, and use the day end to grade the player's actions and, using key flagged actions (as a suggestion: timing when completed could affect endings too - in time, late, way too late, done wrong, etc), lead them towards whatever multiple endings are created in the next (probably third) game.

The only thing puzzling about “The Operator” is why it has so many positive reviews. It’s too simple to deserve the “Investigation” or “Detective” tags. At heart, it’s an atmospheric, highly polished point-and-click adventure, closer to a children’s interactive TV show than an actual investigation puzzle game.

review:
The Operator is a 5/10 for me. I just didn’t like it, and the ending honestly pissed me off. It felt dumb. I went into this game thinking I’d be connecting the dots, using my brain, cracking a case, or at least acting like the man in the chair. I expected some detective-style depth, and yeah, I knew there’d be a story, but not this kind of story.

Gameplay & Expectations
I watched the trailer, played the demo, and at first I was excited. The gameplay itself was fun for what it was, and I thought it would build into something bigger. Instead, it just… ended. The ending was surprising, sure, but it wasn’t good. It left me feeling like all that build-up led nowhere.

Replay Value
There’s barely any replay value. No unlimited mode, no side content, nothing to keep you going after finishing the story. And if I remember correctly, there’s not much you can do to actually change the ending, so I had zero motivation to replay it.

Final Thoughts
It’s a fun little game on sale, but I’d recommend watching a video and playing the demo before you consider buying it. Once I beat it, I felt completely done with
